questions.e: Lambda automatically sends anything the code writes to stdout, stderr or logging frameworks to CloudWatch Logs, so putting logging statements for errors in the function code lets administrators troubleshoot. The SQS queue, SNS topic or Events trigger options add extra services and still require code or configuration that is not needed for basic error logging. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is writing an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application data is stored in an Amazon DynamoDB table and records are constantly updated by all instances. An instance sometimes retrieves old data. The Developer wants to correct this by making sure the reads are strongly consistent. How can the Developer accomplish this?
o: Set ConsistentRead to true when calling GetItem.
Create a new DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) table.
Set Consistency to strong when calling UpdateTable.
Use the GetShardIterator command.
questions.e: DynamoDB reads are eventually consistent by default and can return stale data. Setting ConsistentRead to true on GetItem (or Query/Scan) returns the most recent write. DAX serves eventually consistent reads from cache, UpdateTable has no consistency setting, and GetShardIterator is a DynamoDB Streams call. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has an application that must accept a large amount of incoming data streams and process the data before sending it to many downstream users. Which serverless solution should the Developer use to meet these requirements?
o: Amazon RDS MySQL stored procedure with AWS Lambda.
AWS Direct Connect with AWS Lambda.
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with AWS Lambda.
Amazon EC2 bash script with AWS Lambda.
questions.e: Kinesis Data Streams ingests large volumes of streaming data, and Lambda can consume the shards to process records, with multiple consumers able to read the stream for downstream users; this is fully serverless. RDS stored procedures, Direct Connect (a network link) and EC2 bash scripts are neither serverless ingestion services nor appropriate here. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application is experiencing performance issues based on increased demand. This increased demand is on read-only historical records pulled from an Amazon RDS-hosted database with custom views and queries. A Developer must improve performance without changing the database structure. Which approach will improve performance and MINIMIZE management overhead?
o: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB, move all the data, and point to DynamoDB.
Deploy Amazon ElastiCache for Redis and cache the data for the application.
Deploy Memcached on Amazon EC2 and cache the data for the application.
Deploy Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) on Amazon RDS to improve cache performance.
questions.e: ElastiCache for Redis is a managed cache that offloads repeated read-only queries from RDS without changing the database structure and with little management. Moving to DynamoDB means restructuring custom views and queries, running Memcached on EC2 adds management work, and DAX only works with DynamoDB, not RDS. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has an Amazon DynamoDB table that must be in provisioned mode to comply with user requirements. The application needs to support the following: Average item size: 10 KB. Item reads each second: 10 strongly consistent. Item writes each second: 2 transactional. Which read and write capacity cost-effectively meets these requirements?
o: Read 10; write 2.
Read 30; write 40.
Use on-demand scaling.
Read 300; write 400.
questions.e: A strongly consistent read of a 10 KB item uses 3 RCUs (4 KB units rounded up), so 10 reads per second need 30 RCUs. A transactional write costs twice the normal 10 WCUs per 10 KB item, so 2 per second need 2 x 2 x 10 = 40 WCUs. On-demand mode is ruled out by the requirement, and 10/2 is too low while 300/400 is overprovisioned. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company wants to containerize an existing three-tier web application and deploy it to Amazon ECS Fargate. The application is using session data to keep track of user activities. Which approach would provide the BEST user experience?
o: Provision a Redis cluster in Amazon ElastiCache and save the session data in the cluster.
Create a session table in Amazon Redshift and save the session data in the database table.
Enable session stickiness in the existing Network Load Balancer and manage the session data in the container.
Use an Amazon S3 bucket as data store and save the session data in the bucket.
questions.e: Fargate containers are ephemeral, so session data should be stored externally. ElastiCache for Redis gives fast, shared, durable session storage so any container can serve any user. Redshift and S3 are too slow for session lookups, and sticky sessions with in-container state lose sessions when a task stops or scales in. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application is using a single-node Amazon ElastiCache for Redis instance to improve read performance. Over time, demand for the application has increased exponentially, which has increased the load on the ElastiCache instance. It is critical that this cache layer handles the load and is resilient in case of node failures. What can the Developer do to address the load and resiliency requirements?
o: Add a read replica instance.
Migrate to a Memcached cluster.
Migrate to an Amazon Elasticsearch Service cluster.
Vertically scale the ElastiCache instance.
questions.e: Adding a read replica spreads read load and gives a failover target, because ElastiCache for Redis with replication can promote the replica if the primary fails. Memcached has no replication or failover, Elasticsearch Service is a different service, and scaling a single node vertically adds capacity but not resilience. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is investigating an application's performance issues. The application consists of hundreds of microservices, and a single API call can potentially have a deep call stack. The Developer must isolate the component that is causing the issue. Which AWS service or feature should the Developer use to gather information about what is happening and isolate the fault?
o: AWS X-Ray.
VPC Flow Logs.
Amazon GuardDuty.
Amazon Macie.
questions.e: AWS X-Ray traces requests as they flow through many microservices, builds a service map and shows latency and errors per component, which isolates the faulty service in a deep call stack. VPC Flow Logs show network traffic, GuardDuty detects threats, and Macie discovers sensitive data in S3. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Company runs continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines for its application on AWS CodePipeline. A Developer must write unit tests and run them as part of the pipelines before staging the artifacts for testing. How should the Developer incorporate unit tests as part of CI/CD pipelines?
o: Create a separate CodePipeline pipeline to run unit tests.
Update the AWS CodeBuild specification to include a phase for running unit tests.
Install the AWS CodeDeploy agent on an Amazon EC2 instance to run unit tests.
Create a testing branch in AWS CodeCommit to run unit tests.
questions.e: CodeBuild runs build commands defined in buildspec.yml, so you add a phase (for example in the build or test phase) that runs unit tests; if tests fail the build and the pipeline stage fail. A separate pipeline, a CodeDeploy agent or a testing branch do not integrate tests into the same pipeline before staging artifacts. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application has the following requirements: Performance efficiency of seconds with up to a minute of latency. The data storage size may grow up to thousands of terabytes. Per-message sizes may vary between 100 KB and 100 MB. Data can be stored as key/value stores supporting eventual consistency. What is the MOST cost-effective AWS service to meet these requirements?
o: Amazon DynamoDB.
Amazon S3.
Amazon RDS (with a MySQL engine).
Amazon ElastiCache.
questions.e: Note: the marked answer may be wrong. Messages up to 100 MB exceed the DynamoDB 400 KB item size limit, and S3 stores objects of this size at petabyte scale cheaply with eventual-consistency-style key/value access (key to object). Amazon S3 is the most cost-effective choice, whereas RDS and ElastiCache are not suited to thousands of terabytes. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer must allow guest users without logins to access an Amazon Cognito-enabled site to view files stored within an Amazon S3 bucket. How should the Developer meet these requirements?
o: Create a blank user ID in a user pool, add to the user group, and grant access to AWS resources.
Create a new identity pool, enable access to unauthenticated identities, and grant access to AWS resources.
Create a new user pool, enable access to authenticated identifies, and grant access to AWS resources.
Create a new user pool, disable authentication access, and grant access to AWS resources.
questions.e: A Cognito identity pool can enable unauthenticated (guest) identities and issue temporary AWS credentials with an IAM role that grants read access to the S3 bucket. User pools handle sign-up and sign-in of real users and do not give AWS resource access by themselves, and there is no blank user ID or disabled-authentication feature. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has written code for an application and wants to share it with other Developers on the team to receive feedback. The shared application code needs to be stored long-term with multiple versions and batch change tracking. Which AWS service should the Developer use?
o: AWS CodeBuild.
Amazon S3.
AWS CodeCommit.
AWS Cloud9.
questions.e: AWS CodeCommit is a managed Git repository service that stores code long term with full version history, branches and change tracking, and is easy to share with teammates. CodeBuild compiles and tests code, S3 can store files but lacks Git-style change tracking, and Cloud9 is a cloud IDE. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has discovered that an application responsible for processing messages in an Amazon SQS queue is routinely falling behind. The application is capable of processing multiple messages in one execution, but is only receiving one message at a time. What should the Developer do to increase the number of messages the application receives?
o: Call the ChangeMessageVisibility API for the queue and set MaxNumberOfMessages to a value greater than the default of 1.
Call the AddPermission API to set MaxNumberOfMessages for the ReceiveMessage action to a value greater than the default of 1.
Call the ReceiveMessage API to set MaxNumberOfMessages to a value greater than the default of 1.
Call the SetQueueAttributes API for the queue and set MaxNumberOfMessages to a value greater than the default of 1.
questions.e: ReceiveMessage accepts a MaxNumberOfMessages parameter (1 to 10, default 1), so the consumer should request more messages per call. ChangeMessageVisibility changes the invisibility timeout, AddPermission manages queue permissions, and SetQueueAttributes cannot set MaxNumberOfMessages because it is a per-request parameter. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer registered an AWS Lambda function as a target for an Application Load Balancer (ALB) using a CLI command. However, the Lambda function is not being invoked when the client sends requests through the ALB. Why is the Lambda function not being invoked?
o: A Lambda function cannot be registered as a target for an ALB.
A Lambda function can be registered with an ALB using AWS Management Console only.
The permissions to invoke the Lambda function are missing.
Cross-zone is not enabled on the ALB.
questions.e: When you register a Lambda function with an ALB target group through the CLI, you must also add a resource-based permission (lambda add-permission) so elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com can invoke it; the console adds that automatically. Lambda can be an ALB target by CLI too, and cross-zone load balancing is unrelated. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company provides APIs as a service and commits to a service level agreement (SLA) with all its users. To comply with each SLA, what should the company do?
o: Enable throttling limits for each method in Amazon API Gateway.
Create a usage plan for each user and request API keys to access the APIs.
Enable API rate limiting in Amazon Cognito for each user.
Enable default throttling limits for each stage after deploying the APIs.
questions.e: Usage plans with API keys let you set per-client throttling and quotas so each customer receives what their SLA promises. Method-level or stage-level throttling applies to everyone and cannot differentiate per user, and Cognito has no per-user API rate limiting feature. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is preparing a deployment package using AWS CloudFormation. The package consists of two separate templates: one for the infrastructure and one for the application. The application has to be inside the VPC that is created from the infrastructure template. How can the application stack refer to the VPC created from the infrastructure template?
o: Use the Ref function to import the VPC into the application stack from the infrastructure template.
Use the export flag in the infrastructure template, and then use the Fn::ImportValue function in the application template.
Use the DependsOn attribute to specify that the application instance depends on the VPC in the application template.
Use the Fn::GetAtt function to include the attribute of the VPC in the application template.
questions.e: Export the VPC ID as an output in the infrastructure stack and reference it in the application template with Fn::ImportValue, which is how CloudFormation shares values across stacks. Ref and Fn::GetAtt only work on resources within the same template, and DependsOn orders resources within a stack and cannot import values. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer needs to create an application that supports Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and Facebook authentication. It must also allow access to AWS services, such as Amazon DynamoDB. Which AWS service or feature will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of additional coding?
o: AWS AppSync.
Amazon Cognito identity pools.
Amazon Cognito user pools.
Amazon Lambda@Edge.
questions.e: Cognito identity pools federate identities from SAML providers and social providers such as Facebook and return temporary AWS credentials for services like DynamoDB, with little code. User pools authenticate users but do not directly grant AWS service access, AppSync is a GraphQL service, and Lambda@Edge runs code at CloudFront. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is trying to monitor an application's status by running a cron job that returns 1 if the service is up and 0 if the service is down. The Developer created code that uses an AWS CLI put-metric-alarm command to publish the custom metrics to Amazon CloudWatch and create an alarm. However, the Developer is unable to create an alarm as the custom metrics do not appear in the CloudWatch console. What is causing this issue?
o: Sending custom metrics using the CLI is not supported.
The Developer needs to use the put-metric-data command.
The Developer must use a unified CloudWatch agent to publish custom metrics.
The code is not running on an Amazon EC2 instance.
questions.e: put-metric-alarm creates an alarm on an existing metric; it does not publish data. To publish custom metric values you use put-metric-data. A custom metric then appears in CloudWatch and the alarm can monitor it. The CLI does support custom metrics, the CloudWatch agent is optional, and code may run anywhere with credentials. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has written an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances and generates a value every minute. The Developer wants to monitor and graph the values generated over time without logging in to the instance each time. Which approach should the Developer use to achieve this goal?
o: Use the Amazon CloudWatch metrics reported by default for all EC2 instances. View each value from the CloudWatch console.
Develop the application to store each value in a file on Amazon S3 every minute with the timestamp as the name.
Publish each generated value as a custom metric to Amazon CloudWatch using available AWS SDKs.
Store each value as a variable and add the variable to the list of EC2 metrics that should be reported to the Amazon CloudWatch console.
questions.e: Custom values generated by an application are published to CloudWatch as custom metrics using the SDK (PutMetricData), then graphed in the console without logging in. Default EC2 metrics do not include application values, S3 files are not graphable, and you cannot simply add a variable to the default metric list. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Development team decides to adopt a continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) process using AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeCommit for a new application. However, management wants a person to review and approve the code before it is deployed to production. How can the Development team add a manual approver to the CI/CD pipeline?
o: Use AWS SES to send an email to approvers when their action is required. Develop a simple application that allows approvers to accept or reject a build. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to advance the pipeline when a build is accepted.
If approved, add an approved tag when pushing changes to the CodeCommit repository. CodePipeline will proceed to build and deploy approved commits without interruption.
Add an approval step to CodeCommit. Commits will not be saved until approved.
Add an approval action to the pipeline. Configure the approval action to publish to an Amazon SNS topic when approval is required. The pipeline execution will stop and wait for an approval.
questions.e: In CodePipeline you add a manual approval action; it can publish a notification to an SNS topic, and the pipeline pauses until an approver approves or rejects. CodeCommit has no approval step for commits, tags do not control pipeline flow, and a custom SES app plus Lambda is unnecessary work. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is building a serverless application using AWS Lambda and must create a REST API using an HTTP GET method. What needs to be defined to meet this requirement? (Choose TWO)
o: A Lambda@Edge function.
An Amazon API Gateway with a Lambda function.
An exposed GET method in an Amazon API Gateway.
An exposed GET method in the Lambda function.
An exposed GET method in Amazon Route 53.
questions.e: A REST API with a GET method is created by defining an API Gateway API with a Lambda integration and exposing a GET method on a resource. Lambda functions have no HTTP method exposure of their own, Route 53 is DNS, and Lambda@Edge runs functions at CloudFront edge locations rather than defining a REST API. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is writing an application in AWS Lambda. To simplify testing and deployments, the Developer needs the database connection string to be easily changed without modifying the Lambda code. How can this requirement be met?
o: Store the connection string as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager.
Store the connection string in an IAM user account.
Store the connection string in AWS KMS.
Store the connection string as a Lambda layer.
questions.e: AWS Secrets Manager stores the connection string outside the code so it can be changed per environment without redeploying; the function reads it at runtime (Parameter Store would also work). IAM users hold identities, KMS stores keys rather than application values, and a Lambda layer would still be packaged code. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is launching an ecommerce website and will host the static data in Amazon S3. The company expects approximately 1,000 transactions per second (TPS) for GET and PUT requests in total. Logging must be enabled to track all requests and must be retained for auditing purposes. What is the MOST cost-effective solution?
o: Enable AWS CloudTrail logging for the S3 bucket-level action and create a lifecycle policy to move the data from the log bucket to Amazon S3 Glacier in 90 days.
Enable S3 server access logging and create a lifecycle policy to expire the data in 90 days.
Enable AWS CloudTrail logging for the S3 bucket-level action and create a lifecycle policy to expire the data in 90 days.
Enable S3 server access logging and create a lifecycle policy to move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier in 90 days.
questions.e: S3 server access logging is free apart from storage of the log files, and a lifecycle policy to Glacier keeps them cheaply for auditing. CloudTrail data events for S3 at 1,000 requests per second are expensive, and expiring logs after 90 days would not retain them for auditing. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer decides to store highly secure data in Amazon S3 and wants to implement server-side encryption (SSE) with granular control of who can access the master key. Company policy requires that the master key be created, rotated, and disabled easily when needed, all for security reasons. Which solution should be used to meet these requirements?
o: SSE with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
SSE with AWS KMS managed keys (SSE-KMS).
SSE with AWS Secrets Manager.
SSE with customer-provided encryption keys.
questions.e: SSE-KMS uses KMS keys that you control with key policies, rotate, disable and audit, which gives granular access control over the master key. SSE-S3 keys are managed entirely by S3, SSE-C requires you to supply and manage keys with each request, and Secrets Manager is not an S3 encryption option. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is migrating an on-premises application to AWS. The application currently takes user uploads and saves them to a local directory on the server. All uploads must be saved and made immediately available to all instances in an Auto Scaling group. Which approach will meet these requirements?
o: Use Amazon EBS and configure the application AMI to use a snapshot of the same EBS instance on boot.
Use Amazon S3 and rearchitect the application so all uploads are placed in S3.
Use instance storage and share it between instances launched from the same Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
Use Amazon EBS and file synchronization software to achieve eventual consistency among the Auto Scaling group.
questions.e: Amazon S3 is shared, durable storage that every instance sees immediately, so rearchitecting the app to write uploads to S3 meets the requirement. EBS volumes attach to a single instance, instance store is ephemeral and not shared, and synchronizing files between instances is only eventually consistent. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer implemented a static website hosted in Amazon S3 that makes web service requests hosted in Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The site is showing an error that reads: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is present on the requested resource. Origin null is therefore not allowed access.' What should the Developer do to resolve this issue?
o: Enable cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) on the S3 bucket.
Enable cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) for the method in API Gateway.
Add the Access-Control-Request-Method header to the request.
Add the Access-Control-Request-Headers header to the request.
questions.e: The error means the browser blocked a cross-origin call to API Gateway because the response lacked CORS headers. Enabling CORS on the API method (and deploying the API) makes it return Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Enabling CORS on the S3 bucket affects requests to S3, not the API, and the Request headers are set by the browser. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is building an application that needs to store data in Amazon S3. Management requires that the data be encrypted before it is sent to Amazon S3 for storage. The encryption keys need to be managed by the Security team. Which approach should the Developer take to meet these requirements?
o: Implement server-side encryption using customer-provided encryption keys (SSE-C).
Implement server-side encryption by using a client-side master key.
Implement client-side encryption using an AWS KMS managed customer master key (CMK).
Implement client-side encryption using Amazon S3 managed keys.
questions.e: The data must be encrypted before sending to S3, which is client-side encryption, and a KMS-managed key lets the Security team control the key. SSE-C and server-side encryption options encrypt after the data reaches S3, and S3-managed keys are not controlled by the security team. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has written an Amazon Kinesis Data Streams application. As usage grows and traffic increases over time, the application is regularly receiving ProvisionedThroughputExceededException error messages. Which steps should the Developer take to resolve the error? (Choose TWO)
o: Use Auto Scaling to scale the stream for better performance.
Increase the delay between the GetRecords call and the PutRecords call.
Increase the number of shards in the data stream.
Specify a shard iterator using the ShardIterator parameter.
Implement exponential backoff on the GetRecords call and the PutRecords call.
questions.e: ProvisionedThroughputExceededException means the stream's shard limits are exceeded. Increase the number of shards for more capacity, and retry with exponential backoff on GetRecords and PutRecords. Kinesis Data Streams does not auto scale in provisioned mode, and a delay between calls or a shard iterator parameter does not solve limit errors. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is publishing critical log data to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs, which was created 2 months ago. The Developer must encrypt the log data using an AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) so future data can be encrypted to comply with the company's security policy. How can the Developer meet this requirement?
o: Use the CloudWatch Logs console and enable the encrypt feature on the log group.
Use the AWS CLI create-log-group command and specify the key Amazon Resource Name (ARN).
Use the KMS console and associate the CMK with the log group.
Use the AWS CLI associate-kms-key command and specify the key Amazon Resource Name (ARN)
questions.e: Encryption can be added to an existing log group by using the AWS CLI associate-kms-key command with the KMS key ARN; future data is then encrypted. The console and KMS console cannot encrypt an existing log group this way, and create-log-group with a key ARN applies only when creating a new log group. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has code running on Amazon EC2 instances that needs read-only access to an Amazon DynamoDB table. What is the MOST secure approach the Developer should take to accomplish this task?
o: Create a user access key for each EC2 instance with read-only access to DynamoDB. Place the keys in the code. Redeploy the code as keys rotate.
Use an IAM role with an AmazonDynamoDBReadOnlyAccess policy applied to the EC2 instances.
Run all code with only AWS account root user access keys to ensure maximum access to services.
Use an IAM role with Administrator access applied to the EC2 instance.
questions.e: An IAM role attached to the EC2 instance supplies temporary credentials automatically, and AmazonDynamoDBReadOnlyAccess provides least privilege read access. Embedding access keys in code, using root keys or granting administrator access are insecure and violate least privilege. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer migrated a web application to AWS. As part of the migration, the Developer implemented an automated continuous integration/continuous improvement (CI/CD) process using a blue/green deployment. The deployment provisions new Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a new Application Load Balancer. After the migration was completed, the Developer began receiving complaints from users getting booted out of the system. The system also requires users to log in after every new deployment. How can these issues be resolved?
o: Use rolling updates instead of a blue/green deployment.
Externalize the user sessions to Amazon ElastiCache.
Turn on sticky sessions in the Application Load Balancer.
Use multicast to replicate session information.
questions.e: Sessions kept on individual instances are lost when blue/green deployment replaces the fleet. Externalizing session state to a shared store such as ElastiCache keeps sessions across deployments and instances. Sticky sessions and rolling updates still tie sessions to instances, and multicast replication is not supported in AWS VPC. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer wants to insert a record into an Amazon DynamoDB table as soon as a new file is added to an Amazon S3 bucket. Which set of steps would be necessary to achieve this?
o: Create an event with Amazon CloudWatch Events that will monitor the S3 bucket and then insert the records into DynamoDB.
Configure an S3 event to invoke a Lambda function that inserts records into DynamoDB.
Create a Lambda function that will poll the S3 bucket and then insert the records into DynamoDB.
Create a cron job that will run at a scheduled time and insert the records into DynamoDB.
questions.e: S3 event notifications can invoke a Lambda function when an object is created, and the function writes the record to DynamoDB. CloudWatch Events cannot directly insert records, and polling with Lambda or cron jobs is inefficient and does not react as soon as the file is added. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has implemented AWS CodeDeploy as part of its cloud native CI/CD stack. The company enables automatic rollbacks while deploying a new version of a popular web application from in-place to Amazon EC2. What occurs if the deployment of the new version fails due to code regression?
o: The last known good deployment is automatically restored using the snapshot stored in Amazon S3.
CodeDeploy switches the Amazon Route 53 alias records back to the known good green deployment and terminates the failed blue deployment.
A new deployment of the last known version of the application is deployed with a new deployment ID.
AWS CodePipeline promotes the most recent deployment with a SUCCEEDED status to production.
questions.e: When CodeDeploy rolls back automatically it redeploys the last known good revision as a new deployment with a new deployment ID; it does not restore a snapshot. Route 53 switches and CodePipeline promotion are not what in-place EC2 rollbacks do. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer uses Amazon S3 buckets for static website hosting. The Developer creates one S3 bucket for the code and another S3 bucket for the assets, such as image and video files. Access is denied when a user attempts to access the assets bucket from the code bucket, with the website application showing a 403 error. How should the Developer solve this issue?
o: Create an IAM role and apply it to the assets bucket for the code bucket to be granted access.
Edit the bucket policy of the assets bucket to allow access from the code bucket.
Edit the bucket policy of the assets bucket to open access to all principals.
Change the code bucket to use AWS Lambda functions instead of static website hosting.
questions.e: The website assets bucket denies the request because its policy does not allow it. Editing the assets bucket policy to allow access from the code bucket (or the website origin) solves the 403 while staying controlled. Making it open to all principals is insecure, IAM roles cannot be applied to buckets, and Lambda is not required. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has implemented AWS CodePipeline to automate its release pipelines. The Development team is writing an AWS Lambda function what will send notifications for state changes of each of the actions in the stages. Which steps must be taken to associate the Lambda function with the event source?
o: Create a trigger that invokes the Lambda function from the Lambda console by selecting CodePipeline as the event source.
Create an event trigger and specify the Lambda function from the CodePipeline console.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors status changes in Code Pipeline and triggers the Lambda function.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch Events rule that uses CodePipeline as an event source.
questions.e: CodePipeline emits state-change events to CloudWatch Events (EventBridge), so you create a rule with CodePipeline as the event source and the Lambda function as the target. The Lambda console and CodePipeline console do not provide a direct trigger for pipeline state changes, and a CloudWatch alarm is for metrics. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has built an application running on AWS Lambda using AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM). What is the correct order of execution to successfully deploy the application?
o: 1. Build the SAM template in Amazon EC2. 2. Package the SAM template to Amazon EBS storage. 3. Deploy the SAM template from Amazon EBS.
1. Build the SAM template locally. 2. Package the SAM template onto Amazon S3. 3. Deploy the SAM template from Amazon S3.
1. Build the SAM template locally. 2. Deploy the SAM template from Amazon S3. 3. Package the SAM template for use.
1. Build the SAM template locally. 2. Package the SAM template from AWS CodeCommit. 3. Deploy the SAM template to CodeCommit.
questions.e: SAM deployment is build locally, package (upload artifacts to S3 and produce a transformed template), then deploy from S3 through CloudFormation. EC2, EBS and CodeCommit are not used for the SAM package and deploy flow. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company wants to migrate an imaging service to Amazon EC2 while following security best practices. The images are sourced and read from a non-public Amazon S3 bucket. What should a Developer do to meet these requirements?
o: Create an IAM user with read-only permissions for the S3 bucket. Temporarily store the user credentials in the Amazon EBS volume of the EC2 instance.
Create an IAM user with read-only permissions for the S3 bucket. Temporarily store the user credentials in the user data of the EC2 instance.
Create an EC2 service role with read-only permissions for the S3 bucket. Attach the role to the EC2 instance.
Create an S3 service role with read-only permissions for the S3 bucket. Attach the role to the EC2 instance.
questions.e: An IAM role for EC2 with read-only access to the S3 bucket, attached to the instance, provides temporary credentials without storing keys. IAM user credentials stored on an EBS volume or in user data are insecure, and there is no S3 service role that EC2 can use. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Development team wants to immediately build and deploy an application whenever there is a change to the source code. Which approaches could be used to trigger the deployment? (Choose TWO)
o: Store the source code in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS CodePipeline to start whenever a file in the bucket changes.
Store the source code in an encrypted Amazon EBS volume. Configure AWS CodePipeline to start whenever a file in the volume changes.
Store the source code in an AWS CodeCommit repository. Configure AWS CodePipeline to start whenever a change is committed to the repository.
Store the source code in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS CodePipeline to start every 15 minutes.
Store the source code in an Amazon EC2 instance's ephemeral storage. Configure the instance to start AWS CodePipeline whenever there are changes to the source code.
questions.e: CodePipeline can start automatically when a change is made in an S3 bucket (source action with versioning) or when a commit is pushed to CodeCommit. EBS volumes and EC2 ephemeral storage are not supported sources, and a 15-minute schedule is not immediate. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application ingests a large number of small messages and stores them in a database. The application uses AWS Lambda. A Development team is making changes to the application's processing logic. In testing, it is taking more than 15 minutes to process each message. The team is concerned the current backend may time out. Which changes should be made to the backend system to ensure each message is processed in the MOST scalable way?
o: Add the messages to an Amazon SQS queue. Set up and Amazon EC2 instance to poll the queue and process messages as they arrive.
Add the messages to an Amazon SQS queue. Set up Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to poll the queue and process the messages as they arrive.
Create a support ticket to increase the Lambda timeout to 60 minutes to allow for increased processing time.
Change the application to directly insert the body of the message into an Amazon RDS database.
questions.e: Lambda has a 15 minute maximum timeout that cannot be extended by a support ticket. Putting the messages in SQS and having EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group poll the queue scales with load and can run longer than 15 minutes. A single instance does not scale, and RDS inserts do not address processing time. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Software Engineer developed an AWS Lambda function in Node.js to do some CPU-intensive data processing. With the default settings, the Lambda function takes about 5 minutes to complete. Which approach should a Developer take to increase the speed of completion?
o: Instead of using Node.js, rewrite the Lambda function using Python.
Instead of packaging the libraries in the ZIP file with the function, move them to a Lambda layer and use the layer with the function.
Allocate the maximum available CPU units to the function.
Increase the available memory to the function.
questions.e: In Lambda CPU power is allocated in proportion to memory, so increasing memory speeds up CPU-intensive work. You cannot allocate CPU units directly, changing language is not guaranteed to help, and moving libraries to a layer does not change execution speed. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An online retail company has deployed a serverless application with AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon S3, and Amazon DynamoDB using AWS CloudFormation. The company rolled out a new release with major upgrades to the Lambda function and deployed the release to production. Subsequently, the application stopped working. Which solution should bring the application back up as quickly as possible?
o: Redeploy the application on Amazon EC2 so the Lambda function can resolve dependencies.
Migrate DynamoDB to Amazon RDS and redeploy the Lambda function.
Roll back the Lambda function to the previous version.
Deploy the latest Lambda function in a different Region.
questions.e: Lambda keeps versions, so rolling the function back to the previous version (alias or version pointer) restores service quickly. Moving to EC2, migrating DynamoDB to RDS or deploying in another Region are slow changes that do not address the faulty release. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is writing an application that will run on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The Developer wants to externalize session state to support the application. Which services will meet these needs? (Choose TWO)
o: Amazon DynamoDB.
Amazon Cognito.
Amazon ElastiCache.
Amazon EBS.
Amazon SQS.
questions.e: Session state can be externalized in a fast shared store: ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) or DynamoDB, both accessible by every instance. Cognito handles identity, EBS volumes attach to a single instance, and SQS is a message queue, not a session store. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has a legacy application that is hosted on-premises. Other applications hosted on AWS depend on the on-premises application for proper functioning. In case of any application errors, the Developer wants to be able to use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor and troubleshoot all applications from one place. How can the Developer accomplish this?
o: Install an AWS SDK on the on-premises server to automatically send logs to CloudWatch.
Download the CloudWatch agent to the on-premises server. Configure the agent to use IAM user credentials with permissions for CloudWatch.
Upload log files from the on-premises server to Amazon S3 and have CloudWatch read the files.
Upload log files from the on-premises server to an Amazon EC2 instance and have the instance forward the logs to CloudWatch.
questions.e: The CloudWatch agent can run on on-premises servers; configured with IAM user credentials that have CloudWatch permissions, it sends logs and metrics to CloudWatch so all applications are monitored in one place. An SDK would not automatically send logs, and S3 or EC2 forwarding adds unnecessary steps. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is developing an application that will be accessed through the Amazon API Gateway REST API. Registered users should be the only ones who can access certain resources of this API. The token being used should expire automatically and needs to be refreshed periodically. How can a Developer meet these requirements?
o: Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool, configure the Amazon Cognito Authorizer in API Gateway, and use the temporary credentials generated by the identity pool.
Create and maintain a database record for each user with a corresponding token and use an AWS Lambda authorizer in API Gateway.
Create an Amazon Cognito user pool, configure the Cognito Authorizer in API Gateway, and use the identity or access token.
Create an IAM user for each API user, attach an invoke permissions policy to the API, and use an IAM authorizer in API Gateway.
questions.e: A Cognito user pool with a Cognito authorizer on API Gateway lets only registered users call the API using identity or access tokens, which expire and can be refreshed. Identity pools issue AWS credentials rather than tokens for this authorizer, and custom token databases or IAM users per API user are unnecessary overhead. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is working on a serverless project based in Java. Initial testing shows a cold start takes about 8 seconds on average for AWS Lambda functions. What should the Developer do to reduce the cold start time? (Choose TWO)
o: Add the Spring Framework to the project and enable dependency injection.
Reduce the deployment package by including only needed modules from the AWS SDK for Java.
Increase the memory allocation setting for the Lambda function.
Increase the timeout setting for the Lambda function.
Change the Lambda invocation mode from synchronous to asynchronous.
questions.e: Smaller deployment packages that include only needed SDK modules reduce load time on cold start, and more memory also means more CPU, which speeds initialization. A heavy framework like Spring slows startup, timeout does not affect init speed, and asynchronous invocation does not change cold starts. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is leveraging a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP)-based AWS VPN connection to connect from on-premises to Amazon EC2 instances in the Developer's account. The Developer is able to access an EC2 instance in subnet A, but is unable to access an EC2 instance in subnet B in the same VPC. Which logs can the Developer use to verify whether the traffic is reaching subnet B?
o: VPN logs.
BGP logs
VPC Flow Logs.
AWS CloudTrail logs.
questions.e: VPC Flow Logs capture IP traffic to and from network interfaces, so they show whether packets from the on-premises network reach the instance in subnet B and whether they are accepted or rejected. VPN and BGP logs show tunnel state and routes, and CloudTrail logs API activity only. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has created a new AWS IAM user that has s3:putObject permission to write to a specific Amazon S3 bucket. This S3 bucket uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed keys (SSE-KMS) as the default encryption. Using the access key and secret key of the IAM user, the application received an access denied error when calling the PutObject API. How can this issue be resolved?
o: Update the policy of the IAM user to allow the s3:EncryptionConfiguration action.
Update the bucket policy of the S3 bucket to allow the IAM user to upload objects.
Update the policy of the IAM user to allow the kms:GenerateDataKey action.
Update the ACL of the S3 bucket to allow the IAM user to upload objects.
questions.e: With SSE-KMS as the bucket default, the uploader needs permission to use the KMS key, such as kms:GenerateDataKey (and kms:Decrypt for multipart), to encrypt the object. S3 permissions alone are not enough. The bucket policy, ACL or s3:EncryptionConfiguration permissions do not grant KMS key use. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has a web application that uses an Amazon Cognito user pool for authentication. The company wants to create a login page with the company logo. What should a Developer do to meet these requirements?
o: Create a hosted user interface in Amazon Cognito and customize it with the company logo.
Create a login page with the company logo and upload it to Amazon Cognito.
Create a login page in Amazon API Gateway with the logo and save the link in Amazon Cognito.
Upload the logo to the Amazon Cognito app settings and point to the logo on a custom login page.
questions.e: Cognito provides a hosted UI for user pools that you can customize with a logo and CSS, so no separate login page needs to be built. You cannot upload your own login page into Cognito, and API Gateway or app settings do not provide that capability. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is working on an AWS Lambda function that accesses Amazon DynamoDB. The Lambda function must retrieve an item and update some of its attributes, or create the item if it does not exist. The Lambda function has access to the primary key. Which IAM permissions should the Developer request for the Lambda function to achieve this functionality?
o: dynamodb:DeleteItem dynamodb:GetItem dynamodb:PutItem.
dynamodb:UpdateItem dynamodb:GetItem dynamodb:DescribeTable.
dynamodb:GetRecords dynamodb:PutItem dynamodb:UpdateTable.
dynamodb:UpdateItem dynamodb:GetItem dynamodb:PutItem.
questions.e: To update an item or create it if it does not exist, the function needs dynamodb:UpdateItem and PutItem, plus GetItem to retrieve it. DeleteItem, DescribeTable, GetRecords and UpdateTable are not needed for this get-or-create-and-update workflow. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is storing sensitive data generated by an application in Amazon S3. The Developer wants to encrypt the data at rest. A company policy requires an audit trail of when the master key was used and by whom. Which encryption option will meet these requirements?
o: Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
Server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed keys (SSE-KMS).
Server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C).
Server-side encryption with self-managed keys.
questions.e: SSE-KMS uses a KMS key and every use of the key is logged in CloudTrail, showing when and by whom, which meets the audit requirement. SSE-S3 keys are not visible to you, and with SSE-C or self-managed keys AWS has no record of key usage. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company's website runs on an Amazon EC2 instance and uses Auto Scaling to scale the environment during peak times. Website users across the world are experiencing high latency due to static content on the EC2 instance, even during non-peak hours. Which combination of steps will resolve the latency issue? (Choose TWO)
o: Double the Auto Scaling group's maximum number of servers.
Host the application code on AWS Lambda.
Scale vertically by resizing the EC2 instances.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache the static content.
Store the application's static content in Amazon S3.
questions.e: Store the static content in S3 and put a CloudFront distribution in front, so global users are served from edge locations with lower latency and the EC2 instances are offloaded. Scaling servers, resizing instances or using Lambda does not reduce geographic latency. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is developing a web application that allows its employees to upload a profile picture to a private Amazon S3 bucket. There is no size limit for the profile pictures, which should be displayed every time an employee logs in. For security reasons, the pictures cannot be publicly accessible. What is a viable long-term solution for this scenario?
o: Generate a presigned URL when a picture is uploaded. Save the URL in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Return the URL to the browser when the employee logs in.
Save the picture's S3 key in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint to allow the employees to download pictures once they log in.
Encode a picture using base64. Save the base64 string in an Amazon DB table. Allow the browser to retrieve the string and convert it to a picture.
Save the picture's S3 key in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use a function to generate a presigned URL every time an employee logs in. Return the URL to the browser.
questions.e: Store only the object key in DynamoDB and generate a presigned URL at each login, so the URL is fresh and the bucket remains private. A saved presigned URL would expire, a VPC endpoint does not give browsers access, and base64 in a database is not viable with no size limit. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is going to deploy an AWS Lambda function that requires significant CPU utilization. Which approach will MINIMIZE the average runtime of the function?
o: Deploy the function into multiple AWS Regions.
Deploy the function into multiple Availability Zones.
Deploy the function using Lambda layers.
Deploy the function with its memory allocation set to the maximum amount.
questions.e: Lambda allocates CPU in proportion to memory, so setting the memory to the maximum gives the most CPU and shortens the runtime of CPU-heavy functions. Multiple Regions or AZs do not make a single invocation faster, and layers only package dependencies. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has a legacy application that was migrated to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application stores data in a MySQL database that is currently installed on a single EC2 instance. The company has decided to migrate the database from the EC2 instance to MySQL on Amazon RDS. What should the Developer do to update the application to support data storage in Amazon RDS?
o: Update the database connection parameters in the application to point to the new RDS instance.
Add a script to the EC2 instance that implements an AWS SDK for requesting database credentials.
Create a new EC2 instance with an IAM role that allows access to the new RDS database.
Create an AWS Lambda function that will route traffic, from the EC2 instance to the RDS database.
questions.e: Moving to RDS MySQL just needs the application to connect to the new endpoint, so update the connection parameters (host, credentials) in the application. No SDK credential script, new IAM role or Lambda proxy is required for a standard MySQL connection. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has an e-commerce API hosted on Amazon ECS. Variable and spiking demand on the application is causing order processing to take too long. The application processes Amazon SQS queues. The ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric spikes at very high values throughout the day, which cause Amazon CloudWatch alarm breaches. Other ECS metrics for the API containers are well within limits. What can the Developer implement to improve performance while keeping costs low?
o: Target tracking scaling policy.
Docker Swarm.
Service scheduler.
Step scaling policy.
questions.e: A target tracking scaling policy automatically adjusts the number of ECS tasks to hold a target value for a metric such as queue depth per task, which handles spiky demand with low management and cost. Step scaling needs manual thresholds, Docker Swarm is not an AWS service for this, and the service scheduler only maintains a desired count. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer wants to build an application that will allow new users to register and create new user accounts. The application must also allow users with social media accounts to log in using their social media credentials. Which AWS service or feature can be used to meet these requirements?
o: AWS IAM.
Amazon Cognito identity pools.
Amazon Cognito user pools.
AWS Directory Service.
questions.e: Cognito user pools provide sign-up and sign-in for new users and support social identity providers such as Facebook and Google. Identity pools give AWS credentials, IAM manages AWS identities, and Directory Service is for directories like Active Directory. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company wants to implement authentication for its new REST service using Amazon API Gateway. To authenticate the calls, each request must include HTTP headers with a client ID and user ID. These credentials must be compared to authentication data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. What MUST the company do to implement this authentication in API Gateway?
o: Implement an AWS Lambda authorizer that references the DynamoDB authentication table.
Create a model that requires the credentials, then grant API Gateway access to the authentication table.
Modify the integration requests to require the credentials, then grant API Gateway access to the authentication table.
Implement an Amazon Cognito authorizer that references the DynamoDB authentication table.
questions.e: A Lambda authorizer (custom authorizer) can read the headers from the request, check them against DynamoDB and return an IAM policy. Models, integration requests and Cognito authorizers cannot query a DynamoDB table for custom header credentials. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is trying to make API calls using SDK. The IAM user credentials used by the application require multi-factor authentication for all API calls. Which method the Developer use to access the multi-factor authentication protected API?
o: GetFederationToken.
GetCallerIdentity.
GetSessionToken.
DecodeAutherizationMessage.
questions.e: GetSessionToken returns temporary credentials for an IAM user and can include an MFA device serial number and code, so it is used to call APIs that require MFA. GetFederationToken is for federated users, GetCallerIdentity returns who you are, and DecodeAuthorizationMessage decodes error messages. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application is running on a cluster of Amazon EC2 instances. While trying to read objects stored within a single Amazon S3 bucket that are encrypted with server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed keys (SSE-KMS), the application receives the following error. Which combination of steps should be taken to prevent this failure? (Choose TWO)
o: Contact AWS Support to request an AWS KMS rate limit increase.
Perform error retries with exponential backoff in the application code.
Contact AWS Support to request a S3 rate limit increase.
Import a customer master key (CMK) with a larger key size.
Use more than one customer master key (CMK) to encrypt S3 data.
questions.e: The error is a ThrottlingException from AWS KMS: every SSE-KMS read makes a KMS call, and the cluster exceeds the KMS request quota. Request a KMS rate limit increase and add retries with exponential backoff. The throttling comes from KMS, not S3, and a larger imported key size does not change request rates. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: When developing an AWS Lambda function that processes Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Administrators within the company must receive a notice that includes the processed data. How should the Developer write the function to send processed data to the Administrators?
o: Separate the Lambda handler from the core logic.
Use Amazon CloudWatch Events to send the processed data.
Publish the processed data to an Amazon SNS topic.
Push the processed data to Amazon SQS.
questions.e: A Lambda function can publish the processed data to an SNS topic, to which administrators are subscribed by email or SMS, so they get a notice with the data. Separating handler and logic is just code structure, CloudWatch Events does not carry the data, and SQS requires administrators to poll. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is storing sensitive documents in Amazon S3 that will require encryption at rest. The encryption keys must be rotated annually, at least. What is the easiest way to achieve this?
o: Encrypt the data before sending it to Amazon S3.
Import a custom key into AWS KMS with annual rotation enabled.
Use AWS KMS with automatic key rotation.
Export a key from AWS KMS to encrypt the data.
questions.e: AWS KMS customer managed keys support automatic annual rotation that you just enable, which is the easiest approach. Encrypting data yourself, importing key material (which does not auto-rotate) or exporting keys (not possible from KMS) add work or are impossible. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is creating a REST service using an Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda integration. The service must run different versions for testing purposes. What would be the BEST way to accomplish this?
o: Use an x-Version header to denote which version is being called and pass that header to the Lambda function(s).
Create an API Gateway Lambda authorizer to route API clients to the correct API version.
Create an API Gateway resource policy to isolate versions and provide context to the Lambda function(s).
Deploy the API versions as unique stages with unique endpoints and use stage variables to provide further context.
questions.e: Deploy each version as a separate API Gateway stage with its own endpoint, and use stage variables to point to the matching Lambda alias or configuration. Custom headers, authorizers or resource policies are not intended to route between API versions. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer must encrypt a 100-GB object using AWS KMS. What is the BEST approach?
o: Make an Encrypt API call to encrypt the plaintext data as ciphertext using a customer master key (CMK).
Make an Encrypt API call to encrypt the plaintext data as ciphertext using a customer master key (CMK) with imported key material.
Make an GenerateDataKey API call that returns a plaintext key and an encrypted copy of a data key. Use a plaintext key to encrypt the data.
Make an GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext API call that returns an encrypted copy of a data key. Use an encrypted key to encrypt the data.
questions.e: KMS Encrypt can handle only up to 4 KB of data, so for a 100 GB object you call GenerateDataKey (envelope encryption), encrypt the data locally with the plaintext key and store the encrypted data key with it. GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext gives you no usable plaintext key to encrypt with. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Development team would like to migrate their existing application code from a GitHub repository to AWS CodeCommit. What needs to be created before they can migrate a cloned repository to CodeCommit over HTTPS?
o: A GitHub secure authentication token.
A public and private SSH key file.
A set of Git credentials generated from IAM.
An Amazon EC2 IAM role with CodeCommit permissions.
questions.e: To access CodeCommit over HTTPS you generate Git credentials (username and password) for an IAM user. A GitHub token authenticates to GitHub, SSH keys are for the SSH protocol, and an EC2 role is for instances. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: What item operation allows the retrieval of multiple items from a DynamoDB table in a single API call?
o: GetItem.
BatchGetItem.
GetMultipleItems.
GetItemRange.
questions.e: BatchGetItem retrieves multiple items (up to 100 items, 16 MB) from one or more tables in a single API call. GetItem returns only one item, and GetMultipleItems and GetItemRange do not exist. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: After launching an instance that you intend to serve as a NAT (Network Address Translation) device in a public subnet you modify your route tables to have the NAT device be the target of internet bound traffic of your private subnet. When you try and make an outbound connection to the Internet from an instance in the private subnet, you are not successful. NAT device be the target of internet bound traffic of your private subnet. Which of the following steps could resolve the issue?
o: Attaching a second Elastic Network interface (ENI) to the NAT instance, and placing it in the private subnet.
Attaching a second Elastic Network Interface (ENI) to the instance in the private subnet, and placing it in the public subnet.
Disabling the Source/Destination Check attribute on the NAT instance.
Attaching an Elastic IP address to the instance in the private subnet.
questions.e: A NAT instance forwards traffic not addressed to itself, so the Source/Destination Check attribute must be disabled on it; otherwise it drops traffic. Adding ENIs or Elastic IPs to the private instance does not fix the routing path. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: You attempt to store an object in the US-STANDARD region in Amazon S3, and receive a confirmation that it has been successfully stored. You then immediately make another API call and attempt to read this object. S3 tells you that the object does not exist. What could explain this behavior?
o: US-STANDARD uses eventual consistency and it can take time for an object to be readable in a bucket.
Objects in Amazon S3 do not become visible until they are replicated to a second region.
US-STANDARD imposes a 1 second delay before new objects are readable.
ou exceeded the bucket object limit, and once this limit is raised the object will be visible.
questions.e: Note: the marked answer may be wrong. It reflects the old eventual consistency model for new objects; Amazon S3 now provides strong read-after-write consistency for all PUTs, so a successfully stored object is immediately readable. The listed answer was correct for older S3 behavior, and US-STANDARD is no longer a region name. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: What is the maximum number of S3 Buckets available per AWS account?
o: 100 per region.
there is no limit.
1,000,000 per account.
500 per account.
100 per IAM user.
questions.e: The marked answer reflects the current S3 quota where an account can have up to 1,000,000 general purpose buckets (default is lower and can be raised by request). Older documentation said 100 buckets per account, which is why the other options are wrong, and the limit is per account not per region or IAM user. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following items are required to allow an application deployed on an EC2 instance to write data to a DynamoDB table? Assume that no security Keys are allowed to be stored on the EC2 instance. (Choose TWO)
o: Create an IAM User that allows write access to the DynamoDB table.
Add an IAM Role to a running EC2 instance.
Add an IAM User to a running EC2 Instance.
Launch an EC2 Instance with the IAM Role included in the launch configuration.
Create an IAM Role that allows write access to the DynamoDB table.
Launch an EC2 Instance with the IAM User included in the launch configuration.
questions.e: Without storing keys, the instance gets permissions from an IAM role: create a role that allows DynamoDB write access and launch the instance with that role (instance profile). IAM users require access keys on the instance, which violates the constraint. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following are correct statements with policy evaluation logic in AWS Identity and Access Management? (Choose TWO)
o: By default, all requests are denied.
An explicit allow overrides an explicit deny.
An explicit allow overrides default deny.
An explicit deny does not override an explicit allow.
By default, all request are allowed.
questions.e: IAM evaluation begins with an implicit default deny for all requests, and an explicit allow overrides that default deny. An explicit deny overrides any explicit allow, so the options saying otherwise are wrong, and requests are not allowed by default. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: You have an environment that consists of a public subnet using Amazon VPC and 3 instances that are running in this subnet. These three instances can successfully communicate with other hosts on the Internet. You launch a fourth instance in the same subnet, using the same AMI and security group configuration you used for the others, but find that this instance cannot be accessed from the Internet. What should you do to enable internet access?
o: Deploy a NAT instance into the public subnet.
Modify the routing table for the public subnet.
Configure a publically routable IP Address In the host OS of the fourth instance.
Assign an Elastic IP address to the fourth instance.
questions.e: An instance in a public subnet needs a public IP to be reachable from the internet; the other three instances have one. Assigning an Elastic IP to the fourth instance fixes it. A NAT instance serves private subnets, the route table is already shared with the working instances, and OS-level IPs cannot be public. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: If a message is retrieved from a queue in Amazon SQS, how long is the message inaccessible to other users by default?
o: 0 seconds.
1 hour.
1 day.
forever.
30 seconds.
questions.e: The default SQS visibility timeout is 30 seconds, during which a received message is hidden from other consumers. If it is not deleted by then, it becomes visible again. It can be set from 0 seconds up to 12 hours. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: What is the format of structured notification messages sent by Amazon SNS?
o: An XML object containing Messageld, UnsubscribeURL, Subject, Message and other values.
An JSON object containing Messageld, DuplicateFlag, Message and other values.
An XML object containing Messageld, DuplicateFlag, Message and other values.
An JSON object containing Messageld, unsubscribeURL, Subject, Message and other values.
questions.e: SNS sends structured notifications as a JSON object that contains fields such as MessageId, Subject, Message, Timestamp and UnsubscribeURL. SNS notification messages are not XML objects and do not use a DuplicateFlag. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: When uploading an object, what request header can be explicitly specified in a request to Amazon S3 to encrypt object data when saved on the server side?
o: x-amz-storage-class.
Content-MD5.
x-amz-security-token.
x-amz-server-side-encryption.
questions.e: To request server-side encryption on upload, the x-amz-server-side-encryption request header is used (for example AES256 or aws:kms). x-amz-storage-class chooses the storage class, Content-MD5 is an integrity check, and x-amz-security-token carries temporary credentials. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following platforms are supported by Elastic Beanstalk? (Choose TWO)
o: Apache Tomcat.
.NET.
IBM Websphere.
Oracle JBoss.
Jetty.
questions.e: Elastic Beanstalk supports platforms including Apache Tomcat (Java) and .NET (IIS on Windows), along with Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby, Go and Docker. IBM WebSphere, Oracle JBoss and Jetty are not supported platforms. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which code snippet below returns the URL of a load balanced web site created in CloudFormation with an AWS::ElasticLoadBalancing::LoadBalancer resource name ElasticLoad Balancer?
o: "Fn::Join":[ "".["http://", {Fn::GetAtt": [ "ElasticLoadBalancer","DNSName"]}]].
"Fn::Join":[ "".["http://", {Fn::GetAtt": [ "ElasticLoadBalancer","Url"]}]].
"Fn::Join":[ "".["http://", {"Ref : "ElasticLoadBalancerUrl"}]].
"Fn::Join":[ "".["http://", {"Ref : "ElasticLoadBalancer","DNSName"}]].
questions.e: A load balancer's DNS name is exposed through the DNSName attribute, so Fn::GetAtt with ElasticLoadBalancer and DNSName inside Fn::Join with http:// produces the site URL. There is no Url attribute, and Ref on a classic load balancer returns its name, not a URL. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which features can be used to restrict access to data in S3? (Choose TWO)
o: Use S3 Virtual Hosting.
Set an S3 Bucket policy.
Enable IAM Identity Federation.
Set an S3 ACL on the bucket or the object.
Create a CloudFront distribution for the bucket.
questions.e: Access to S3 data can be restricted with bucket policies and with ACLs on the bucket or object. Virtual hosting is just URL style, IAM federation is for identities not data restriction, and CloudFront distributes content rather than restricting direct S3 access by itself. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: What happens, by default, when one of the resources in a CloudFormation stack cannot be created?
o: Previously-created resources are kept but the stack creation terminates.
Previously-created resources are deleted and the stack creation terminates.
The stack creation continues, and the final results indicate which steps failed.
CloudFormation templates are parsed in advance so stack creation is guaranteed to succeed.
questions.e: By default CloudFormation rolls back on failure: if a resource cannot be created, the stack creation stops and the previously created resources are deleted. Rollback can be disabled, but that is not the default, and templates are not guaranteed to succeed. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following are valid arguments for an SNS Publish request? (Choose THREE)
o: TopicArn.
Subject.
Destination.
Format.
Message.
Language.
questions.e: An SNS Publish request takes TopicArn (or TargetArn), Message and optionally Subject, among others like MessageStructure and MessageAttributes. Destination, Format and Language are not valid Publish arguments. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: How can software determine the public and private IP addresses of the Amazon EC2 instance that it is running on?
o: Query the appropriate Amazon CloudWatch metric.
Use ipconfig or ifconfig command.
Query the local instance userdata.
Query the local instance metadata.
questions.e: An EC2 instance can query the instance metadata service (http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) to get its public and private IP addresses. User data holds launch scripts, CloudWatch metrics do not list IPs, and ifconfig would not show the public IP. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: EC2 instances are launched from Amazon Machine images (AMIs). A given public AMI can:
o: Be used to launch EC2 Instances in any AWS region.
Only be used to launch EC2 instances in the same country as the AMI is stored.
Only be used to launch EC2 instances in the same AWS region as the AMI is stored.
Only be used to launch EC2 instances in the same AWS availability zone as the AMI is stored.
questions.e: AMIs are regional resources, so an AMI can be used to launch instances only in the Region where it is stored, though it can be copied to other Regions. It is not tied to a single Availability Zone or country. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which EC2 API call would you use to retrieve a list of Amazon Machine Images (AMIs)?
o: DescribeInstances.
DescribeAMIs.
DescribeImages.
GetAMIs.
You cannot retrieve a list of AMIs as there are over 10,000 AMIs.
questions.e: The EC2 DescribeImages API call returns a list of AMIs available to you. DescribeInstances lists instances, and DescribeAMIs and GetAMIs do not exist. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: In AWS, which security aspects are the customer's responsibility? (Choose FOUR)
o: Life-cycle management of IAM credentials.
Decommissioning storage devices.
Security Group and ACL (Access Control List) settings.
Encryption of EBS (Elastic Block Storage) volumes.
Controlling physical access to compute resources.
Patch management on the EC2 instance's operating system.
questions.e: Under the shared responsibility model the customer manages IAM credential lifecycle, security group and network ACL settings, EBS volume encryption and operating system patching on EC2. AWS handles physical access and decommissioning of storage devices. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: When using a large Scan operation in DynamoDB, what technique can be used to minimize the impact of a scan on a table's provisioned throughput?
o: Set a smaller page size for the scan.
Use parallel scans.
Define a range index on the table.
Prewarm the table by updating all items.
questions.e: A large Scan can consume a table's capacity in bursts, so use a smaller page size (limit) and let the Scan return fewer items per request, which spreads the load. Parallel scans increase consumption, and range indexes or updating items do not help. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: How can you secure data at rest on an EBS volume?
o: Attach the volume to an instance using EC2's SSL interface.
Write the data randomly instead of sequentially.
Use an encrypted file system on top of the EBS volume.
Encrypt the volume using the S3 server-side encryption service.
Create an IAM policy that restricts read and write access to the volume.
questions.e: To protect data at rest on EBS, you encrypt with an encrypted file system on top of the volume (or use EBS encryption). SSL does not encrypt at rest, S3 SSE does not apply to EBS, and IAM policies limit access but do not encrypt data. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following is chosen as the default region when making an API call with an AWS SDK?
o: ap-northeast-1.
us-west-2.
us-east-1.
eu-west-1.
us-central-1.
questions.e: If no Region is configured, the AWS SDKs use us-east-1 (N. Virginia) as the default for API calls. Other Regions require explicit configuration, and us-central-1 is not a valid Region. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about SWF are true? (Choose THREE)
o: SWF tasks are assigned once and never duplicated.
SWF requires an S3 bucket for workflow storage.
SWF workflow executions can last up to a year.
SWF triggers SNS notifications on task assignment.
SWF uses deciders and workers to complete tasks.
SWF requires at least 1 EC2 instance per domain.
questions.e: SWF assigns tasks once and never duplicates them, executions can run up to a year, and workflows use deciders and workers to complete tasks. SWF does not need an S3 bucket or EC2 instances per domain, and it does not trigger SNS notifications on assignment. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A startup s photo-sharing site is deployed in a VPC. An ELB distributes web traffic across two subnets. ELB session stickiness is configured to use the AWS-generated session cookie, with a session TTL of 5 minutes.
