The webserver Auto Scaling Group is configured as: min-size=4, max-size=4, The startups preparing for a public launch, by running load-testing software installed on a single EC2 instance running in us-west-2. After 60 minutes of load-testing, the webserver logs show. Which recommendations can help ensure load-testing HTTP requests are evenly distributed across the four webservers? (Choose TWO)
o: Launch and run the load-tester EC2 instance from us-east-1 instead.
Re-configure the load-testing software to re-resolve DNS for each web request.
Use a 3rd-party load-testing service which offers globally-distributed test clients.
Configure ELB and Auto Scaling to distribute across us-west-2a and us-west-2c.
Configure ELB session stickiness to use the app-specific session cookie.
questions.e: The logs show the load tester hit only two servers in us-west-2a because it resolves the ELB DNS once and uses a single source IP, so requests concentrate on one ELB node. Re-resolving DNS per request or using distributed test clients spreads traffic across all ELB nodes and servers. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following are valid SNS delivery transports? (Choose TWO)
o: HTTP.
UDP.
SMS.
DynamoDB.
Named Pipes.
questions.e: SNS delivers notifications over transports such as HTTP/HTTPS, email, SMS, SQS, Lambda and mobile push. UDP, DynamoDB and named pipes are not valid SNS delivery transports. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Company C has recently launched an online commerce site for bicycles on AWS. They have a Product DynamoDB table that stores details for each bicycle, such as, manufacturer, color, price, quantity and size to display in the online store. Due to customer demand, they want to include an image for each bicycle along with the existing details. Which approach below provides the least impact to provisioned throughput on the Product table?
o: Serialize the image and store it in multiple DynamoDB tables.
Create an Images DynamoDB table to store the Image with a foreign key constraint to the Product table.
Add an image data type to the Product table to store the images in binary format.
Store the images in Amazon S3 and add an S3 URL pointer to the Product table item for each image.
questions.e: Storing large images in DynamoDB would consume lots of read and write capacity and exceeds the 400 KB item limit. Putting images in S3 and keeping only the S3 URL in the Product item adds almost no throughput load. DynamoDB has no foreign key constraints. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which DynamoDB limits can be raised by contacting AWS support? (Choose TWO)
o: The number of hash keys per account.
The maximum storage used per account.
The number of tables per account.
The number of local secondary indexes per account.
The number of provisioned throughput units per account.
questions.e: The number of tables per account and the provisioned throughput units per account are soft limits that AWS Support can raise. Items such as hash keys, local secondary indexes per table and storage are not limited in the way described. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: When a Simple Queue Service message triggers a task that takes 5 minutes to complete, which process below will result in successful processing of the message and remove it from the queue while minimizing the chances of duplicate processing?
o: Retrieve the message with an increased visibility timeout, process the message, delete the message from the queue.
Retrieve the message with an increased visibility timeout, delete the message from the queue, process the message.
Retrieve the message with increased DelaySeconds, process the message, delete the message from the queue.
Retrieve the message with increased DelaySeconds, delete the message from the queue, process the message.
questions.e: Set an increased visibility timeout when retrieving the message so it stays hidden for the 5 minutes of processing, process it, then delete it after success. Deleting before processing risks losing the task, and DelaySeconds only delays the message becoming available. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Company A has an S3 bucket containing premier content that they intend to make available to only paid subscribers of their website. The S3 bucket currently has default permissions of all objects being private to prevent inadvertent exposure of the premier content to non-paying website visitors. How can Company A provide only paid subscribers the ability to download a premier content file in the S3 bucket?
o: Apply a bucket policy that grants anonymous users to download the content from the S3 bucket.
Generate a pre-signed object URL for the premier content file when a paid subscriber requests a download.
Add a bucket policy that requires Multi-Factor Authentication for requests to access the S3 bucket objects.
Enable server side encryption on the S3 bucket for data protection against the non-paying website visitors.
questions.e: A pre-signed URL gives time-limited access to a private object, so Company A generates one for each paying subscriber's request. An anonymous bucket policy exposes content to everyone, MFA is not practical for website visitors, and server-side encryption does not control who can download. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a good DynamoDB hash key schema for provisioned throughput efficiency?
o: User ID, where the application has many different users.
Status Code where most status codes are the same.
Device ID, where one is by far more popular than all the others.
Game Type, where there are three possible game types.
questions.e: A good hash key has many distinct values with an even access pattern, such as User ID with many users, which spreads load across partitions. Keys with few values or one dominant value create hot partitions and waste provisioned throughput. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application stores payroll information nightly in DynamoDB for a large number of employees across hundreds of offices. Item attributes consist of individual name, office identifier, and cumulative daily hours. Managers run reports for ranges of names working in their office. One query is: Return all Items in this office for names starting with A through E. Which table configuration will result in the lowest impact on provisioned throughput for this query?
o: Configure the table to have a hash index on the name attribute, and a range index on the office identifier.
Configure the table to have a range index on the name attribute, and a hash index on the office identifier.
Configure a hash index on the name attribute and no range index.
Configure a hash index on the office identifier attribute and no range index.
questions.e: The query is by office and a name range, so the office identifier is the hash key and name is the range key, allowing a Query with a key condition on the range. Hashing on name or leaving out the range requires scanning more data and consumes more throughput. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: What is one key difference between an Amazon EBS-backed and an instance-store backed instance?
o: Virtual Private Cloud requires EBS backed instances.
Amazon EBS-backed instances can be stopped and restarted.
Auto scaling requires using Amazon EBS-backed instances.
Instance-store backed instances can be stopped and restarted.
questions.e: EBS-backed instances can be stopped and restarted, preserving the root volume, while instance store-backed instances cannot be stopped (only rebooted or terminated). VPC and Auto Scaling do not require EBS-backed instances. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following services are included at no additional cost with the use of the AWS platform?
o: Simple Storage Service.
Elastic Compute Cloud.
Auto Scaling.
Elastic Load Balancing.
CloudFormation.
Simple Workflow Service.
questions.e: Auto Scaling and CloudFormation have no additional charge; you pay only for the resources they create. S3, EC2, Elastic Load Balancing and SWF are billed services. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Your application is trying to upload a 6 GB file to Simple Storage Service and receive a Your proposed upload exceeds the maximum allowed object size. error message. What is a possible solution for this?
o: None, Simple Storage Service objects are limited to 5 GB.
Use the multi-part upload API for this object.
Use the large object upload API for this object.
Contact support to increase your object size limit.
Upload to a different region.
questions.e: S3 single PUT uploads are limited to 5 GB, but objects can be up to 5 TB using the multipart upload API, so use multipart for a 6 GB file. There is no large object API and support cannot raise the limit; the region does not matter. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: What AWS products and features can be deployed by Elastic Beanstalk? (Choose THREE)
o: Auto scaling groups.
Route 53 hosted zones.
Elastic Load Balancers.
RDS Instances.
Elastic IP addresses.
SQS Queues.
questions.e: Elastic Beanstalk can provision Auto Scaling groups, Elastic Load Balancers and RDS instances as part of an environment. It does not deploy Route 53 hosted zones, Elastic IP addresses or SQS queues as environment resources. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Games-R-Us is launching a new game app for mobile devices. Users will log into the game using their existing Facebook account and the game will record player data and scoring information directly to a DynamoDB table. What is the most secure approach for signing requests to the DynamoDB API?
o: Create an IAM user with access credentials that are distributed with the mobile app to sign the requests.
Distribute the AWS root account access credentials with the mobile app to sign the requests.
Request temporary security credentials using web identity federation to sign the requests.
Establish cross account access between the mobile app and the DynamoDB table to sign the requests
questions.e: Use web identity federation: the app signs users in through Facebook and exchanges the token for temporary AWS security credentials (with Cognito or STS) to sign DynamoDB requests. Embedding IAM user or root credentials in a mobile app is insecure, and cross-account access does not apply. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following programming languages have an officially supported AWS SDK? (Choose TWO)
o: Perl.
PHP.
Pascal.
Java.
SQL.
questions.e: AWS officially provides SDKs for languages such as Java, PHP, Python, .NET, Ruby, JavaScript, Go and C++. Perl, Pascal and SQL do not have officially supported AWS SDKs. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A meteorological system monitors 600 temperature gauges, obtaining temperature samples every minute and saving each sample to a DynamoDB table Each sample involves writing 1K of data and the writes are evenly distributed over time. How much write throughput is required for the target table?
o: 1 write capacity unit.
10 write capacity units.
60 write capacity units.
600 write capacity units.
3600 write capacity units.
questions.e: 600 gauges write one sample per minute, which is 600 / 60 = 10 writes per second. Each 1 KB write consumes 1 WCU, so 10 WCUs are required. The other values result from miscalculating the time unit. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: In DynamoDB, what type of HTTP response codes indicate that a problem was found with the client request sent to the service?
o: 5xx HTTP response code.
200 HTTP response code.
306 HTTP response code.
4xx HTTP response code.
questions.e: DynamoDB returns 4xx HTTP status codes for problems with the client request, such as validation errors or throttling. 5xx codes indicate server-side problems, and 200 is success. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Company B provides an online image recognition service and utilizes SQS to decouple system components for scalability The SQS consumers poll the imaging queue as often as possible to keep end-to-end throughput as high as possible. However, Company B is realizing that polling in tight loops is burning CPU cycles and increasing costs with empty responses. How can Company B reduce the number of empty responses?
o: Set the imaging queue visibility Timeout attribute to 20 seconds.
Set the Imaging queue ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds attribute to 20 seconds.
Set the imaging queue MessageRetentionPeriod attribute to 20 seconds.
Set the DelaySeconds parameter of a message to 20 seconds.
questions.e: Setting ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds on the queue enables long polling, which waits up to 20 seconds for a message and reduces empty responses and CPU use. Visibility timeout, retention period and DelaySeconds do not affect how long a receive call waits. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An Amazon S3 bucket, myawsbucket is configured with website hosting in Tokyo region, what is the region-specific website endpoint?
o: www.myawsbucket.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com.
myawsbucket.s3-website-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com.
myawsbucket.amazonaws.com.
myawsbucket.tokyo.amazonaws.com.
questions.e: S3 website endpoints use the format bucket-name.s3-website-region.amazonaws.com, so for Tokyo it is myawsbucket.s3-website-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com. The other options are not valid S3 website endpoint formats. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: You are inserting 1000 new items every second in a DynamoDB table. Once an hour these items are analyzed and then are no longer needed. You need to minimize provisioned throughput, storage, and API calls. Given these requirements, what is the most efficient way to manage these Items after the analysis?
o: Retain the items in a single table.
Delete items individually over a 24 hour period.
Delete the table and create a new table per hour.
Create a new table per hour.
questions.e: Since items are only needed for an hour, create a table per hour and delete the table after analysis. Deleting a table is a single call and releases throughput and storage, while deleting items individually consumes write capacity and API calls, and retaining them costs storage. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: You have written an application that uses the Elastic Load Balancing service to spread traffic to several web servers. Your users complain that they are sometimes forced to login again in the middle of using your application, after they have already logged in. This is not behavior you have designed. What is a possible solution to prevent this happening?
o: Use instance memory to save session state.
Use instance storage to save session state.
Use EBS to save session state.
Use ElastiCache to save session state.
Use Glacier to save session slate.
questions.e: Users are logged out because session state is stored on individual instances behind the load balancer. Storing session state in ElastiCache, a shared external store, lets any server read the session. Instance memory, instance storage and EBS are local, and Glacier is archival storage. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: You run an ad-supported photo sharing website using S3 to serve photos to visitors of your site. At some point you find out that other sites have been linking to the photos on your site, causing loss to your business. What is an effective method to mitigate this?
o: Store photos on an EBS volume of the web server.
Remove public read access and use signed URLs with expiry dates.
Use CloudFront distributions for static content.
Block the IPs of the offending websites in Security Groups.
questions.e: Removing public read access and serving photos through pre-signed URLs with an expiry means other sites can only hotlink links that soon stop working, while your own pages generate fresh URLs. EBS storage on a web server does not stop hotlinking and scales poorly. CloudFront alone still serves public content to anyone. Blocking IPs in security groups is impractical because hotlinking requests come from visitors' browsers, not from the offending servers. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which statements about DynamoDB are true? (Choose TWO)
o: DynamoDB uses a pessimistic locking model.
DynamoDB uses optimistic concurrency control.
DynamoDB uses conditional writes for consistency.
DynamoDB restricts item access during reads.
DynamoDB restricts item access during writes.
questions.e: DynamoDB does not lock items for reads or writes. It uses optimistic concurrency control, where conditional writes (for example, a condition expression on a version attribute) succeed only if the item is still in the expected state, otherwise the write fails and the client retries. Pessimistic locking and restricting item access during reads or writes describe traditional locking databases, not DynamoDB. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: You are providing AWS consulting services for a company developing a new mobile application that will be leveraging Amazon SNS Mobile Push for push notifications. In order to send direct notification messages to individual devices each device registration identifier or token needs to be registered with SNS; however the developers are not sure of the best way to do this. You advise them to:
o: Bulk upload the device tokens contained in a CSV file via the AWS Management Console.
Let the push notification service (e.g. Amazon Device Messaging) handle the registration.
Implement a token vending service to handle the registration.
Call the CreatePlatformEndPoint API function to register multiple device tokens.
questions.e: In SNS Mobile Push, each device token must be registered as a platform endpoint by calling the CreatePlatformEndpoint API against a platform application, and the app or a backend does this when the token is received. The console has no bulk CSV upload for device tokens. The push service only issues tokens and does not register them in SNS. A token vending service is unrelated, since it vends AWS credentials, not SNS endpoints. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: You are writing to a DynamoDB table and receive the following exception: ProvisionedThroughputExceededException. though according to your Cloudwatch metrics for the table, you are not exceeding your provisioned throughput. What could be an explanation for this?
o: You haven't provisioned enough DynamoDB storage instances.
You're exceeding your capacity on a particular Range Key.
You're exceeding your capacity on a particular Hash Key.
You're exceeding your capacity on a particular Sort Key.
You haven't configured DynamoDB Auto Scaling triggers.
questions.e: DynamoDB divides provisioned throughput across partitions, and the partition key (hash key) decides which partition an item lands on. If requests concentrate on one hot partition key, that partition is throttled with ProvisionedThroughputExceededException even though table-wide consumption in CloudWatch looks below the limit. DynamoDB is serverless, so there are no storage instances, and a sort or range key does not define a partition by itself. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: If an application is storing hourly log files from thousands of instances from a high traffic web site, which naming scheme would give optimal performance on S3?
o: Sequential.
instanceID_log-HH-DD-MM-YYYY.
instanceIDLog-YYYY-MM-DD-HH.
HH-DD-MM-YYYY-log_instanceID.
YYYY-MM-DD-HH-logInstanceID.
questions.e: S3 historically partitioned index keys by key prefix, so keys that start with an evenly distributed, non-sequential value such as an instance ID spread load across partitions. Sequential or date-leading prefixes (HH-DD-MM, YYYY-MM-DD) concentrate requests on one partition and hurt performance. Today S3 scales per prefix automatically, but among these options the instance ID prefix is still the best choice. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about SQS is true?
o: Messages will be delivered exactly once and messages will be delivered in First in, First out order.
Messages will be delivered exactly once and message delivery order is indeterminate.
Messages will be delivered one or more times and messages will be delivered in First in, First out order.
Messages will be delivered one or more times and message delivery order is indeterminate.
questions.e: Standard SQS queues give at-least-once delivery, so a message may be delivered more than once, and ordering is best-effort, meaning the order is not guaranteed. Consumers must be idempotent. Exactly-once processing with strict first-in first-out order is only offered by FIFO queues, which is not what these options describe for standard SQS. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A corporate web application is deployed within an Amazon VPC, and is connected to the corporate data center via IPSec VPN. The application must authenticate against the on-premise LDAP server. Once authenticated, logged-in users can only access an S3 keyspace specific to the user. Which two approaches can satisfy the objectives? (Choose TWO)
o: The application authenticates against LDAP. The application then calls the IAM Security Service to login to IAM using the LDAP credentials. The application can use the 1AM temporary credentials to access the appropriate S3 bucket.

The application authenticates against LDAP, and retrieves the name of an IAM role associated with the user. The application then calls the IAM Security Token Service to assume that IAM Role. The application can use the temporary credentials to access the appropriate S3 bucket.
The application authenticates against IAM Security Token Service using the LDAP credentials. The application uses those temporary AWS security credentials to access the appropriate S3 bucket.

Develop an identity broker which authenticates against LDAP, and then calls IAM Security Token Service to get IAM federated user credentials. The application calls the identity broker to get IAM federated user credentials with access to the appropriate S3 bucket.

Develop an identity broker which authenticates against IAM Security Token Service to assume an IAM Role to get temporary AWS security credentials. The application calls the identity broker to get AWS temporary security credentials with access to the appropriate S3 bucket.
questions.e: Both correct options exchange LDAP-authenticated identity for temporary credentials from STS: the app authenticates against LDAP, then uses AssumeRole on a per-user role, or an identity broker calls STS (GetFederationToken) to return scoped federated credentials. IAM and STS cannot authenticate LDAP credentials directly, so the options where the app logs into IAM or STS with LDAP credentials fail. The broker must authenticate against LDAP, not against STS. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Company C is currently hosting their corporate site in an Amazon S3 bucket with Static Website Hosting enabled. Currently, when visitors go to http://www.companyc.com the index.html page is returned. Company C now would like a new page welcome.html to be returned when a visitor enters http://www.companyc.com in the browser. Which of the following steps will allow Company C to meet this requirement? (Choose TWO)
o: Upload an html page named welcome.html to their S3 bucket.
Create a welcome subfolder in their S3 bucket.
Set the Index Document property to welcome.html.
Move the index.html page to a welcome subfolder.
Set the Error Document property to welcome.html.
questions.e: Static website hosting serves whatever object is named in the Index Document setting. To return welcome.html at the root, upload welcome.html to the bucket and change the Index Document property to welcome.html. Subfolders do not change the root document, and the Error Document is only returned for errors such as 404, not for normal requests. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: What type of block cipher does Amazon S3 offer for server side encryption?
o: Triple DES.
Advanced Encryption Standard.
Blowfish.
RC5.
questions.e: Amazon S3 server-side encryption (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS and SSE-C) uses AES-256, the Advanced Encryption Standard block cipher. Triple DES, Blowfish and RC5 are not used by S3 for server-side encryption. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Development team wants to instrument their code to provide more detailed information to AWS X-Ray than simple outgoing and incoming requests. This will generate large amounts of data, so the Development team wants to implement indexing so they can filter the data. What should the Development team do to achieve this?
o: Add annotations to the segment document and the code.
Add metadata to the segment document and the code.
Configure the necessary X-Ray environment variables.
Install required plugins for the appropriate AWS SDK.
questions.e: X-Ray annotations are key-value pairs added to the segment document that are indexed, so you can use them in filter expressions and groups to search traces. Metadata is also added to segments but is not indexed and cannot be used for filtering. Environment variables and SDK plugins configure the SDK and daemon but do not add custom indexed data. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A team of Developers must migrate an application running inside an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment from a Classic Load Balancer to an Application Load Balancer. Which steps should be taken to accomplish the task using the AWS Management Console?
o: 1. Update the application code in the existing deployment. 2. Select a new load balancer type before running the deployment. 3. Deploy the new version of the application code to the environment.

1. Create a new environment with the same configurations except for the load balancer type. 2. Deploy the same application version as used in the original environment. 3. Run the swap-environment-cnames action.
1. Clone the existing environment, changing the associated load balancer type. 2. Deploy the same application version as used in the original environment. 3. Run the swap-environment-cnames action.
1. Edit the environment definitions in the existing deployment. 2. Change the associated load balancer type according to the requirements. 3. Rebuild the environment with the new load balancer type.
questions.e: An Elastic Beanstalk environment cannot change its load balancer type in place from Classic to Application. The supported migration is to create a new environment with the same configuration but an ALB, deploy the same application version, then swap CNAMEs for a cutover with little downtime. Editing, rebuilding or redeploying the existing environment does not change its load balancer type, and cloning copies the existing load balancer type. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company needs a version control system for collaborative software development. Features of the system must include the following: Support for batches of changes across multiple files. Parallel branching Version tracking. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
o: AWS CodePipeline.
Amazon S3.
AWS Code Build.
AWS CodeCommit.
questions.e: AWS CodeCommit is a managed Git service, providing version control with commits of changes across multiple files, branching and history tracking. CodePipeline orchestrates release pipelines, CodeBuild compiles and tests code, and S3 is object storage with only basic object versioning, not branching or multi-file commits. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is using continuous integration and continuous delivery systems. A Developer now needs to automate a software package deployment to both Amazon EC2 instances and virtual servers running on-premises. Which AWS service should be used to accomplish this?
o: AWS CodePipeline.
AWS CodeBuild.
AWS Elastic Beanstalk.
AWS CodeDeploy.
questions.e: AWS CodeDeploy automates application deployments to EC2 instances, on-premises servers, Lambda and ECS. CodePipeline orchestrates stages but does not itself deploy to servers, CodeBuild builds and tests code, and Elastic Beanstalk deploys to AWS-managed environments, not to on-premises servers. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer created a new AWS account and must create a scalable AWS Lambda function that meets the following requirements for concurrent execution: Average execution time of 100 seconds 50 requests per second. Which step must be taken prior to deployment to prevent errors?
o: Implement dead-letter queues to capture invocation errors.
Add an event source from Amazon API Gateway to the Lambda function.
Implement error handling within the application code.
Contact AWS Support to increase the concurrent execution limits.
questions.e: At 50 requests per second with 100 second executions, the function needs about 5000 concurrent executions. A new account has a default regional concurrency limit of 1000 (often lower), so the Developer must request a limit increase through AWS Support before deploying or invocations will be throttled. Dead-letter queues, an API Gateway trigger and code-level error handling do not raise the concurrency ceiling. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is building a three-tier web application that should be able to handle a minimum of 5000 requests per minute. Requirements state that the web tier should be completely stateless while the application maintains session state for the users. How can session data be externalized, keeping latency at the LOWEST possible value?
o: Create an Amazon RDS instance, then implement session handling at the application level to leverage a database inside the RDS database instance for session data storage.

Implement a shared file system solution across the underlying Amazon EC2 instances, then implement session handling at the application level to leverage the shared file system for session data storage.
Create an Amazon ElastiCache Memcached cluster, then implement session handling at the application level to leverage the cluster for session data storage.
Create an Amazon DynamoDB table, then implement session handling at the application level to leverage the table for session data storage.
questions.e: ElastiCache is an in-memory store with sub-millisecond latency, which gives the lowest latency for externalized session state and lets the web tier stay stateless. RDS and shared file systems are slower, and DynamoDB, while fast, has single-digit millisecond latency, which is higher than an in-memory cache. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An Amazon DynamoDB table uses a Global Secondary Index (GSI) to support read queries. The primary table is write-heavy, whereas the GSI is used for read operations. Looking at Amazon CloudWatch metrics, the Developer notices that write operations to the primary table are throttled frequently under heavy write activity. However, write capacity units to the primary table are available and not fully consumed. Why is the table being throttled?
o: The GSI write capacity units are underprovisioned.
There are not enough read capacity units on the primary table.
Amazon DynamoDB Streams is not enabled on the table.
A large write operation is being performed against another table.
questions.e: A GSI has its own provisioned write capacity, and every write to the base table is also propagated to the GSI. If the GSI is under-provisioned, it throttles and back-pressures writes to the base table even when the base table has spare capacity. Read capacity, streams and activity on other tables do not cause this write throttling. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company runs an e-commerce website that uses Amazon DynamoDB where pricing for items is dynamically updated in real time. At any given time, multiple updates may occur simultaneously for pricing information on a particular product. This is causing the original editor's changes to be overwritten without a proper review process. Which DynamoDB write option should be selected to prevent this overwriting?
o: Concurrent writes.
Conditional writes.
Atomic writes.
Batch writes.
questions.e: Conditional writes let an update succeed only if the item still has the expected state (for example, the price or a version attribute is unchanged), so a second editor's write fails instead of silently overwriting the first. This is optimistic locking. Concurrent writes is exactly the problem, atomic writes cover counters, and batch writes just group requests without protecting against overwrites. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has been asked to create an AWS Lambda function that is triggered any time updates are made to items in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The function has been created, and appropriate permissions have been added to the Lambda execution role. Amazon DynamoDB streams have been enabled for the table, but the function is still not being triggered. Which option would enable DynamoDB table updates to trigger the Lambda function?
o: Change the StreamViewType parameter value to NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES for the DynamoDB table.
Configure event source mapping for the Lambda function.
Map an Amazon SNS topic to the DynamoDB streams.
Increase the maximum execution time (timeout) setting of the Lambda function.
questions.e: Enabling a DynamoDB stream only produces the change records. Lambda must be wired to the stream with an event source mapping, which polls the stream and invokes the function. The stream view type only affects record contents, SNS cannot be mapped to a stream directly, and a longer timeout does not create the trigger. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is running a Docker application on Amazon ECS. The application must scale based on user load in the last 15 seconds. How should a Developer instrument the code so that the requirement can be met?
o: Create a high-resolution custom Amazon CloudWatch metric for user activity data, then publish data every 30 seconds.
Create a high-resolution custom Amazon CloudWatch metric for user activity data, then publish data every 5 seconds.
Create a standard-resolution custom Amazon CloudWatch metric for user activity data, then publish data every 30 seconds.
Create a standard-resolution custom Amazon CloudWatch metric for user activity data, then publish data every 5 seconds.
questions.e: Standard-resolution CloudWatch metrics have a minimum period of 60 seconds, so they cannot support scaling on the last 15 seconds. High-resolution custom metrics support periods down to 1 second, but data must be published often enough, so publishing every 5 seconds provides several data points within the 15 second window. Publishing every 30 seconds would leave windows with no data. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company needs to ingest terabytes of data each hour from thousands of sources that are delivered almost continually throughout the day. The volume of messages generated varies over the course of the day. Messages must be delivered in real time for fraud detection and live operational dashboards. Which approach will meet these requirements?
o: Send the messages to an Amazon SQS queue, then process the messages by using a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances.
Use the Amazon S3 API to write messages to an S3 bucket, then process the messages by using Amazon Redshift.
Use AWS Data Pipeline to automate the movement and transformation of data.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Client Library to ingest and deliver messages.
questions.e: Kinesis Data Streams is built for ingesting very high volumes of streaming data from many producers, scales by shards for variable load, and enables real-time consumers such as fraud detection and dashboards via the KCL. SQS with EC2, S3 with Redshift, and Data Pipeline are batch or queue oriented and do not give real-time stream processing at this scale. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer accesses AWS CodeCommit over SSH. The SSH keys configured to access AWS CodeCommit are tied to a user with the following permissions. The Developer needs to create/delete branches. Which specific IAM permissions need to be added, based on the principle of least privilege?
o: "codecommit:CreateBranch" "codecommit:DeleteBranch".
"codecommit:Put*".
"codecommit:Update*".
"codecommit:*".
questions.e: Least privilege means granting only the specific actions needed, which here are codecommit:CreateBranch and codecommit:DeleteBranch. The wildcard options (Put*, Update*, codecommit:*) grant many additional unneeded permissions, and Update* and Put* also do not include DeleteBranch. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An AWS Lambda function must access an external site by using a regularly rotated user name and password. These items must be kept securely and cannot be stored in the function code. What combination of AWS services can be used to accomplish this? (Choose TWO)
o: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.
AWS Trusted Advisor.
AWS KMS.
Amazon GuardDuty.
questions.e: Parameter Store (SecureString) can hold the credentials encrypted with KMS, and AWS KMS provides the key used to encrypt and decrypt them, so nothing is stored in code and values can be changed without redeploying. ACM manages TLS certificates, Trusted Advisor gives account recommendations, and GuardDuty is threat detection, none of which store secrets. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is trying to deploy a serverless application using AWS CodeDeploy. The application was updated and needs to be redeployed. What file does the Developer need to update to push that change through CodeDeploy?
o: dockerrun.aws.json.
buildspec.yml.
appspec.yml.
ebextensions.config.
questions.e: CodeDeploy uses the appspec.yml file in the deployment package to define what to deploy and the lifecycle hooks (for Lambda, the function versions and alias traffic shifting). buildspec.yml is for CodeBuild, dockerrun.aws.json is for Elastic Beanstalk Docker, and .ebextensions config files customize Elastic Beanstalk. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is working on an application that handles 10MB documents that contain highly-sensitive data. The application will use AWS KMS to perform clientside encryption. What steps must be followed?
o: Invoke the Encrypt API passing the plaintext data that must be encrypted, then reference the customer managed key ARN in the KeyId parameter.
Invoke the GenerateRandom API to get a data encryption key, then use the data encryption key to encrypt the data.
Invoke the GenerateDataKey API to retrieve the encrypted version of the data encryption key to encrypt the data.
Invoke the GenerateDataKey API to retrieve the plaintext version of the data encryption key to encrypt the data.
questions.e: KMS Encrypt can only encrypt up to 4 KB of data directly, so a 10 MB document needs envelope encryption. Call GenerateDataKey, which returns a plaintext data key and an encrypted copy. Use the plaintext key to encrypt the data locally, discard it, and store the encrypted key with the data. GenerateRandom does not produce a KMS-protected key, and the encrypted key alone cannot encrypt data. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is building a web application that uses Amazon API Gateway to expose an AWS Lambda function to process requests from clients. During testing, the Developer notices that the API Gateway times out even though the Lambda function finishes under the set time limit. Which of the following API Gateway metrics in Amazon CloudWatch can help the Developer troubleshoot the issue? (Choose TWO)
o: CacheHitCount.
IntegrationLatency.
CacheMissCount.
Latency.
Count.
questions.e: IntegrationLatency measures the time between API Gateway sending a request to the backend and receiving the response, while Latency measures the total time from API Gateway receiving the request to returning the response. Comparing the two shows whether the delay or timeout comes from the integration or from API Gateway itself. Cache hit and miss counts and Count do not show where time is spent. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company needs to distribute firmware updates to its customers around the world. Which service will allow easy and secure control of the access to the downloads at the lowest cost?
o: Use Amazon CloudFront with signed URLs for Amazon S3.
Create a dedicated Amazon CloudFront Distribution for each customer.
Use Amazon CloudFront with AWS Lambda@Edge.
Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda to control access to an S3 bucket.
questions.e: CloudFront with signed URLs in front of S3 gives global low-latency delivery with controlled, time-limited access, and it is a single shared distribution so it is inexpensive. A distribution per customer is costly and hard to manage, Lambda@Edge adds cost and code, and API Gateway with Lambda in front of S3 adds more cost and has payload limits. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application writes items to an Amazon DynamoDB table. As the application scales to thousands of instances, calls to the DynamoDB API generate occasional ThrottlingException errors. The application is coded in a language incompatible with the AWS SDK. How should the error be handled?
o: Add exponential backoff to the application logic.
Use Amazon SQS as an API message bus.
Pass API calls through Amazon API Gateway.
Send the items to DynamoDB through Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
questions.e: When the code cannot use the AWS SDK, which has built-in retries, the application should implement retries with exponential backoff itself to handle throttling errors. SQS, API Gateway and Kinesis Data Firehose add complexity and do not address the throttling at the DynamoDB API call level directly. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An e-commerce web application that shares session state on-premises is being migrated to AWS. The application must be fault tolerant, natively highly scalable, and any service interruption should not affect the user experience. What is the best option to store the session state?
o: Store the session state in Amazon ElastiCache.
Store the session state in Amazon CloudFront.
Store the session state in Amazon S3.
Enable session stickiness using elastic load balancers.
questions.e: Session state should be externalized to a shared, fast, highly available in-memory store, and ElastiCache provides that so any instance can serve any user. CloudFront is a CDN and not a session store, S3 is too slow for session data, and sticky sessions tie users to one instance, which is lost if it fails. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is creating a template that uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy an application. This application is serverless and uses Amazon API Gateway, Amazon DynamoDB, and AWS Lambda. Which tool should the Developer use to define simplified syntax for expressing serverless resources?
o: CloudFormation serverless intrinsic functions.
AWS serverless express.
An AWS serverless application model.
A CloudFormation serverless plugin.
questions.e: The AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM) is an extension of CloudFormation that offers simplified syntax such as AWS::Serverless::Function, Api and SimpleTable for serverless resources, and is transformed into full CloudFormation. The other names are not real tools for this purpose. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has a stateful web server on-premises that is being migrated to AWS. The Developer must have greater elasticity in the new design. How should the Developer re-factor the application to make it more elastic? (Choose TWO)
o: Use pessimistic concurrency on Amazon DynamoDB.
Use Amazon CloudFront with an Auto Scaling group.
Use Amazon CloudFront with an AWS Web Application Firewall.
Store session state data in an Amazon DynamoDB table.
Use an ELB with an Auto Scaling group.
questions.e: To make a stateful server elastic, externalize state by storing session data in DynamoDB so any instance can serve any request, and put instances behind an ELB with an Auto Scaling group so capacity scales out and in. Pessimistic concurrency, CloudFront with a WAF, and CloudFront with Auto Scaling do not remove the state dependency or provide elasticity. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer must analyze performance issues with production-distributed applications written as AWS Lambda functions. These distributed Lambda applications invoke other components that make up the applications. How should the Developer identify and troubleshoot the root cause of the performance issues in production?
o: Add logging statements to the Lambda functions, then use Amazon CloudWatch to view the logs.
Use AWS Cloud Trail and then examine the logs.
Use AWS X-Ray, then examine the segments and errors.
Run Amazon Inspector agents and then analyze performance.
questions.e: AWS X-Ray traces requests across distributed Lambda functions and downstream calls, producing a service map with segments, latency and errors, which lets you locate the root cause of performance problems in production. CloudWatch logs show only individual function output, CloudTrail records API calls, and Inspector assesses vulnerabilities, not performance. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer wants to debug an application by searching and filtering log data. The application logs are stored in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The Developer creates a new metric filter to count exceptions in the application logs. However, no results are returned from the logs. What is the reason that no filtered results are being returned?
o: A setup of the Amazon CloudWatch interface VPC endpoint is required for filtering the CloudWatch Logs in the VPC.
CloudWatch Logs only publishes metric data for events that happen after the filter is created.
The log group for CloudWatch Logs should be first streamed to Amazon Elasticsearch Service before metric filtering returns the results.
Metric data points for logs groups can be filtered only after they are exported to an Amazon S3 bucket.
questions.e: A CloudWatch Logs metric filter only evaluates log events that are ingested after the filter is created, and it does not process existing historical data. So no data points appear for earlier exceptions. The other options describe requirements that do not exist, such as exporting to S3 or Elasticsearch. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: To include objects defined by the AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM) in an AWS CloudFormation template, in addition to Resources, what section MUST be included in the document root?
o: Conditions.
Globals.
Transform.
Properties.
questions.e: A CloudFormation template that uses SAM resources must include the Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31 section at the root, which tells CloudFormation to expand SAM syntax into standard resources. Conditions, Globals and Properties are not the required marker, although Globals is an optional SAM section. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is using Amazon RDS MySQL instances for its application database tier and Apache Tomcat servers for its web tier. Most of the database queries from web applications are repeated read requests. Use of which AWS service would increase in performance by adding in-memory store for repeated read queries?
o: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ.
Amazon SQS.
Amazon ElastiCache.
Amazon RDS read replica.
questions.e: ElastiCache provides an in-memory cache (Redis or Memcached) that can hold results of repeated read queries so the application avoids hitting RDS, which reduces latency and database load. Multi-AZ gives availability, not read performance, SQS is messaging, and a read replica offloads reads but is not an in-memory cache. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is investigating an issue whereby certain requests are passing through an Amazon API Gateway endpoint /MyAPI, but the requests do not reach the AWS Lambda function backing /MyAPI. The Developer found that a second Lambda function sometimes runs at maximum concurrency allowed for the given AWS account. How can the Developer address this issue?
o: Manually reduce the concurrent execution limit at the account level.
Add another API Gateway stage for /MyAPI, and shard the requests.
Configure the second Lambda function's concurrency execution limit.
Reduce the throttling limits in the API Gateway /MyAPI endpoint
questions.e: When the second Lambda function consumes all of the account's concurrency, other functions, including the one behind /MyAPI, get throttled. Setting reserved concurrency on the second function limits how much it can use and guarantees the rest of the pool for others. Lowering the account limit or API Gateway throttling makes it worse, and sharding stages does not change Lambda concurrency. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is migrating a single-server, on-premises web application to AWS. The company intends to use multiple servers behind an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) to balance the load, and will also store session data in memory on the web server. The company does not want to lose that session data if a server fails or goes offline, and it wants to minimize user's downtime. Where should the company move session data to MOST effectively reduce downtime and make users' session data more fault tolerant?
o: An Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster.
A second Amazon EBS volume.
The web server's primary disk.
An Amazon EC2 instance dedicated to session data.
questions.e: Session data should be moved out of web server memory into an external, highly available store such as ElastiCache for Redis, which supports replication and failover, so any server can read the sessions and none are lost when a server fails. EBS volumes, the server's disk and a single dedicated EC2 instance are tied to one machine or are single points of failure. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer created configuration specifications for an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application in a file named healthcheckurl.yaml in the .ebextensions/directory of their application source bundle. The file contains the following: After the application launches, the health check is not being run on the correct path, even though it is valid. What can be done to correct this configuration file?
o: Convert the file to JSON format.
Rename the file to a .config extension.
Change the configuration section from options_settings to resources.
Change the namespace of the option settings to a custom namespace.
questions.e: Elastic Beanstalk only processes configuration files in the .ebextensions folder whose names end in .config (YAML or JSON format). A file named healthcheckurl.yaml is ignored, so it must be renamed healthcheckurl.config. The format is already valid, option_settings is the right section, and the namespace is a standard Elastic Beanstalk one. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has created a Lambda function and is finding that the function is taking longer to complete than expected. After some debugging, the Developer has discovered that increasing compute capacity would improve performance. How can the Developer increase the Lambda compute resources?
o: Run on a larger instance size with more compute capacity.
Increase the maximum execution time.
Specify a larger compute capacity when calling the Lambda function.
Increase the allocated memory for the Lambda function.
questions.e: Lambda does not let you choose CPU directly. You allocate memory, and CPU power, network bandwidth and other resources scale proportionally with it, so increasing memory speeds up compute-bound work. Raising the timeout only allows longer runs, and there are no instance sizes or invocation-time compute parameters. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An e-commerce site allows returning users to log in to display customized web pages. The workflow is shown in the image below. An application is running on EC2 instances. Amazon RDS is used for the database that stores user accounts and preferences. The website freezes or is slow to load while waiting for the login step to complete. The remaining components of the site are well-optimized. Which of the following techniques will resolve this issue? (Select TWO)
o: Implement the user login page as an asynchronous Lambda function.
Use Amazon ElastiCache for MemCached to cache user data.
Use Amazon Application Load Balancer to load balance the traffic to the website.
Call the database asynchronously so the code can continue executing.
Batch login requests from hundreds of users together as a single read request to the database.
questions.e: Caching frequently accessed user data in ElastiCache for Memcached reduces repeated slow database reads during login, and calling the database asynchronously prevents the page from blocking while waiting on the query. A Lambda login function and an ALB do not reduce database wait time, and batching logins into one read is not practical and adds delay. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is building a mobile application and needs any update to user profile data to be pushed to all devices accessing the specific identity. The Developer does not want to manage a back end to maintain the user profile data. What is the MOST efficient way for the Developer to achieve these requirements using Amazon Cognito?
o: Use Cognito federated identities.
Use a Cognito user pool.
Use Cognito Sync.
Use Cognito events.
questions.e: Amazon Cognito Sync stores user profile data in the cloud tied to an identity and synchronizes it across all devices of that identity, pushing updates through silent push notifications, with no backend to manage. Federated identities provide credentials, user pools handle sign-in, and Cognito events are triggers on sync actions, not a data store. Note that Cognito Sync is now superseded by AppSync. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company maintains a REST service using Amazon API Gateway and the API Gateway native API key validation. The company recently launched a new registration page, which allows users to sign up for the service. The registration page creates a new API key using CreateApiKey and sends the new key to the user. When the user attempts to call the API using this key, the user receives a 403 Forbidden error. Existing users are unaffected and can still call the API. What code updates will grant these new users access to the API?
o: The createDeployment method must be called so the API can be redeployed to include the newly created API key.
The updateAuthorizer method must be called to update the API's authorizer to include the newly created API key.
The importApiKeys method must be called to import all newly created API keys into the current stage of the API.
The createUsagePlanKey method must be called to associate the newly created API key with the correct usage plan.
questions.e: With API Gateway native API key validation, a key is only usable if it is associated with a usage plan that includes the API stage. After CreateApiKey, the code must call CreateUsagePlanKey to link the key to the usage plan, otherwise the key is rejected with 403 Forbidden. Redeploying, authorizers and importing keys do not attach the key to a plan. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is writing a mobile application that allows users to view images from an S3 bucket. The users must be able to log in with their Amazon login, as well as Facebook and/or Google accounts. How can the Developer provide this authentication functionality?
o: Use Amazon Cognito with web identity federation.
Use Amazon Cognito with SAML-based identity federation.
Use AWS IAM Access/Secret keys in the application code to allow Get* on the S3 bucket.
Use AWS STS AssumeRole in the application code and assume a role with Get* permissions on the S3 bucket.
questions.e: Amazon Cognito with web identity federation lets users sign in with Amazon, Facebook or Google and exchanges the token for temporary AWS credentials to access S3. SAML federation is for enterprise identity providers, and embedding access keys or calling AssumeRole from the app exposes long-term credentials or cannot authenticate public identities. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer wants access to make the log data of an application running on an EC2 instance available to systems administrators. Which of the following enables monitoring of this metric in Amazon CloudWatch?
o: Retrieve the log data from CloudWatch using the GetMetricData API call.
Retrieve the log data from AWS CloudTrail using the LookupEvents API call.
Launch a new EC2 instance, configure Amazon CloudWatch Events, and then install the application.
Install the Amazon CloudWatch Logs agent on the EC2 instance that the application is running on.
questions.e: To make application log data from an EC2 instance available in CloudWatch, install and configure the CloudWatch Logs agent (or the unified CloudWatch agent) on the instance so it ships log files to CloudWatch Logs. GetMetricData reads metrics only, CloudTrail records API activity, and a new instance with CloudWatch Events does not collect existing application logs. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A nightly batch job loads 1 million new records into a DynamoDB table. The records are only needed for one hour, and the table needs to be empty by the next night's batch job. Which is the MOST efficient and cost-effective method to provide an empty table?
o: Use DeleteItem using a ConditionExpression.
Use BatchWriteItem to empty all of the rows.
Write a recursive function that scans and calls out DeleteItem.
Create and then delete the table after the task has completed.
questions.e: Deleting a table and recreating it is the fastest and cheapest way to empty a table with 1 million items, since deletes of individual items consume write capacity. DeleteItem loops, BatchWriteItem and scan-and-delete are slow and consume lots of write capacity units. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has an application that logs all information to Amazon S3. Whenever there is a new log file, an AWS Lambda function is invoked to process the log files. The code works, gathering all of the necessary information. However, when checking the Lambda function logs, duplicate entries with the same request ID are found. What is causing the duplicate entries?
o: The S3 bucket name was specified incorrectly.
The Lambda function failed, and the Lambda service retired the invocation with a delay.
There was an S3 outage, which caused duplicate entries of the sale log file.
The application stopped intermittently and then resumed.
questions.e: Asynchronous Lambda invocations from S3 are retried when the function returns an error or is throttled, with a delay between attempts. Retries use the same request ID, which explains duplicate log entries with the same ID. A wrong bucket name, an S3 outage or an application stop would not produce repeated invocations with the same request ID. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is providing services to many downstream consumers. Each consumer may connect to one or more services. This has resulted in a complex architecture that is difficult to manage and does not scale well. The company needs a single interface to manage these services to consumers. Which AWS service should be used to refactor this architecture?
o: AWS Lambda.
AWS X-Ray.
Amazon SQS.
Amazon API Gateway.
questions.e: Amazon API Gateway provides a single, managed front door for many backend services, handling routing, authentication, throttling and versioning, so consumers use one interface. Lambda is compute, X-Ray is tracing and SQS is messaging, none of which unify access to multiple services. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is creating a serverless website with content that includes HTML files, images, videos, and JavaScript (client-side scripts). Which combination of services should the Developer use to create the website?
o: Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront.
Amazon EC2 and Amazon ElastiCache.
Amazon ECS and Redis.
AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway.
questions.e: A serverless static website with HTML, images, videos and JavaScript can be hosted in S3 and delivered globally with CloudFront. EC2, ECS with Redis, and Lambda with API Gateway require servers or are for dynamic APIs, not for serving static content. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Development team has pushed out 10 applications running on several Amazon EC2 instances. The Operations team is asking for a graphical representation of one key performance metric for each application. These metrics should be available on one screen for easy monitoring. Which steps should the Developer take to accomplish this using Amazon CloudWatch?
o: Create a custom namespace with a unique metric name for each application.
Create a custom dimension with a unique metric name for each application.
Create a custom event with a unique metric name for each application.
Create a custom alarm with a unique metric name for each application.
questions.e: Publish each application's key metric to a custom CloudWatch namespace, each with a unique metric name, then add those metrics to one dashboard for a single-screen view. Dimensions refine a metric, events are for state changes, and alarms alert on thresholds but do not provide a graphical overview. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is creating an application that will require users to access AWS services and allow them to reset their own passwords. Which of the following would allow the company to manage users and authorization while allowing users to reset their own passwords?
o: Amazon Cognito identify pools and AWS STS.
Amazon Cognito identity pools and AWS IAM.
Amazon Cognito user pools and AWS KMS.
Amazon Cognito user pools and identity pools.
questions.e: Cognito user pools manage users, sign-up and sign-in and support self-service password reset, while identity pools exchange user pool tokens for temporary AWS credentials with IAM roles for authorization to AWS services. Using only identity pools with STS or IAM lacks a user directory, and KMS is unrelated. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has three different environments: Development, QA, and Production. The company wants to deploy its code first in the Development environment, then QA, and then Production. Which AWS service can be used to meet this requirement?
o: Use AWS CodeCommit to create multiple repositories to deploy the application.
Use AWS CodeBuild to create, configure, and deploy multiple build application projects.
Use AWS Data Pipeline to create multiple data pipeline provisions to deploy the application.
Use AWS CodeDeploy to create multiple deployment groups.
questions.e: CodeDeploy deployment groups represent separate target environments, so you can create groups for Development, QA and Production and deploy to them in sequence. CodeCommit is source storage, CodeBuild builds code, and Data Pipeline moves data, so none of those provide environment-staged deployments. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company uses Amazon DynamoDB for managing and tracking orders. The DynamoDB table is partitioned based on the order date. The company receives a huge increase in orders during a sales event, causing DynamoDB writes to throttle, and the consumed throughput is far below the provisioned throughput. According to AWS best practices, how can this issue be resolved with MINIMAL costs?
o: Create a new DynamoDB table for every order date.
Increase the read and write capacity units of the DynamoDB table.
Add a random number suffix to the partition key values.
Add a global secondary index to the DynamoDB table.
questions.e: A date-based partition key causes a hot partition as all writes land on today's date, so throttling happens below provisioned capacity. Adding a random suffix to the partition key (write sharding) spreads writes across partitions at no extra cost. Raising capacity costs more and does not fix the hot key, and a table per date or a GSI do not fix the key distribution. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Development team currently supports an application that uses an in-memory store to save accumulated game results. Individual results are stored in a database. As part of migrating to AWS, the team needs to use automatic scaling. The team knows this will yield inconsistent results. Where should the team store these accumulated game results to BEST allow for consistent results without impacting performance?
o: Amazon S3.
Amazon RDS.
Amazon ElastiCache.
Amazon Kinesis.
questions.e: An in-memory store such as ElastiCache (Redis) provides a shared, central cache that all auto scaled instances can read and update with very fast performance and consistent accumulated results. S3, RDS and Kinesis are either slower or not designed for low-latency accumulated counters. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: In a multi-container Docker environment in AWS Elastic Beanstalk, what is required to configure container instances in the environment?
o: An Amazon ECS task definition.
An Amazon ECS cluster.
A Dockerfile in an application package.
A CLI for Elastic Beanstalk.
questions.e: Elastic Beanstalk multi-container Docker environments use Amazon ECS to coordinate containers, and the containers are defined in a task definition file (Dockerrun.aws.json v2). A cluster is created by Elastic Beanstalk for you, and a Dockerfile is for single-container environments. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance needs to access and make API calls to multiple AWS services. What is the MOST secure way to provide access to the AWS services with MINIMAL management overhead?
o: Use AWS KMS to store and retrieve credentials.
Use EC2 instance profiles.
Use AWS root user to make requests to the application.
Store and retrieve credentials from AWS CodeCommit.
questions.e: An EC2 instance profile attaches an IAM role to the instance, so the application gets automatically rotated temporary credentials through the instance metadata service, with no keys to store or manage. KMS and CodeCommit are not credential stores, and using the root user is highly insecure. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company maintains an application responsible for processing several thousand external callbacks each day. The company's System administrators want to know how many callbacks are being received on a rolling basis, and they want this data available for 10 days. The company also wants the ability to issue automated alerts if the number of callbacks exceeds the defined thresholds. What is the MOST cost-effective way to address the need to track and alert on these statistics?
o: Push callback data to an Amazon RDS database that can be queried to show historical data and to alert on exceeded thresholds.
Push callback data to AWS X-Ray and use AWS Lambda to query, display, and alert on exceeded thresholds.
Push callback data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and invoke an AWS Lambda function that stores data in Amazon DynamoDB and sends the required alerts.
Push callback data to Amazon CloudWatch as a custom metric and use the CloudWatch alerting mechanisms to alert System Administrators.
questions.e: Pushing a count to CloudWatch as a custom metric is cheap, stores data points well past 10 days, and CloudWatch alarms can alert on thresholds with SNS notifications. RDS, X-Ray, or Kinesis with Lambda and DynamoDB add cost and complexity for something CloudWatch does natively. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has a website that is developed in PHP and WordPress and is launched using AWS Elastic Beanstalk. There is a new version of the website that needs to be deployed in the Elastic Beanstalk environment. The company cannot tolerate having the website offline if an update fails. Deployments must have minimal impact and rollback as soon as possible. What deployment method should be used?
o: All at once.
Rolling.
Snapshots.
Immutable.
questions.e: Immutable deployments launch a full new set of instances in a separate Auto Scaling group and only switch over when they are healthy, so the live site stays available if the update fails, and rollback is quick by terminating the new instances. All at once causes downtime, rolling reduces capacity and rolls back slowly, and snapshots is not a deployment policy. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has a multi-tiered web application on AWS. During a recent spike in traffic, one of the primary relational databases on Amazon RDS could not serve all the traffic. Some read queries for repeatedly accessed items failed, so users received error messages. What can be done to minimize the impact on database read queries MOST efficiently during future traffic spikes?
o: Use Amazon S3 to cache database query results.
Use Amazon RDS as a custom origin for Amazon CloudFront.
Use local storage and memory on Amazon EC2 instances to cache data.
Use Amazon ElastiCache in front of the primary database to cache data.
questions.e: Placing ElastiCache in front of RDS caches repeatedly read items in memory so most reads never reach the database, reducing load during spikes. S3 is not a query cache, CloudFront custom origin for RDS is not possible, and local EC2 caches are not shared and are inefficient. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer must build an application that uses Amazon DynamoDB. The requirements state that the items being stored in the DynamoDB table will be 7KB in size and that reads must be strongly consistent. The maximum read rate is 3 items per second, and the maximum write rate is 10 items per second. How should the Developer size the DynamoDB table to meet these requirements?
o: Read: 3 read capacity. unitsWrite: 70 write capacity units.
Read: 6 read capacity. unitsWrite: 70 write capacity units.
Read: 6 read capacity. unitsWrite: 10 write capacity units.
Read: 3 read capacity. unitsWrite: 10 write capacity units.
questions.e: A strongly consistent read of up to 4 KB uses 1 RCU, so a 7 KB item needs 2 RCUs, and 3 items per second needs 6 RCUs. Writes use 1 KB units, so a 7 KB item needs 7 WCUs and 10 items per second needs 70 WCUs. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is creating an AWS Lambda function to process a stream of data from an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream. When the Lambda function parses the data and encounters a missing field, it exits the function with an error. The function is generating duplicate records from the Kinesis stream. When the Developer looks at the stream output without the Lambda function, there are no duplicate records. What is the reason for the duplicates?
o: The Lambda function did not advance the Kinesis stream pointer to the next record after the error.
The Lambda event source used asynchronous invocation, resulting in duplicate records.
The Lambda function did not handle the error, and the Lambda service attempted to reprocess the data.
The Lambda function is not keeping up with the amount of data coming from the stream.
questions.e: When a Lambda function reading a Kinesis stream returns an error, Lambda retries the batch until it succeeds or the data expires, and records that were already processed in the failed batch are processed again, creating duplicates. The function should handle the missing field gracefully instead of failing. Kinesis event sources are not asynchronous, and the stream pointer only advances after success. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is developing an application that will run on several Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group and can access a database running on Amazon EC2. The application needs to store secrets required to connect to the database. The application must allow for periodic secret rotation, and there should be no changes to the application when a secret changes. What is the SAFEST way to meet these requirements?
o: Associate an IAM role to the EC2 instance where the application is running with permission to access the database.
Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with the SecureString data type to store secrets.
Configure the application to store secrets in Amazon S3 object metadata.
Hard code the database secrets in the application code itself.
questions.e: Parameter Store SecureString parameters are encrypted with KMS and fetched by the application at runtime using its IAM role, so values can be updated or rotated without any code changes. Hard-coding secrets, storing them in S3 metadata, or relying only on an instance role does not provide secret storage and rotation. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer writes an AWS Lambda function and uploads the code in a .ZIP file to Amazon S3. The Developer makes changes to the code and uploads a new .ZIP file to Amazon S3. However, Lambda executes the earlier code. How can the Developer fix this in the LEAST disruptive way?
o: Create another Lambda function and specify the new .ZIP file.
Call the update-function-code API.
Remove the earlier .ZIP file first, then add the new .ZIP file.
Call the create-alias API.
questions.e: Uploading a new ZIP to S3 does not change the deployed function, since Lambda copies the code at deployment time. Calling the update-function-code API with the new S3 object redeploys the function code in place with minimal disruption. Creating another function, deleting files or creating an alias does not update the code in the existing function. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An AWS Lambda function must read data from an Amazon RDS MySQL database in a VPC and also reach a public endpoint over the internet to get additional data. Which steps must be taken to allow the function to access both the RDS resource and the public endpoint? (Select TWO)
o: Modify the default configuration for the Lambda function to associate it with an Amazon VPC private subnet.
Modify the default network access control list to allow outbound traffic.
Add a NAT Gateway to the VPC.
Modify the default configuration of the Lambda function to associate it with a VPC public subnet.
Add an environmental variable to the Lambda function to allow outbound internet access.
questions.e: To reach RDS in the VPC, the function must be attached to the VPC, and for internet access it must run in a private subnet whose route table sends outbound traffic to a NAT gateway. Lambda in a public subnet does not get a public IP, so it cannot reach the internet, and NACL changes and environment variables do not provide internet access. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has been asked to make changes to the source code of an AWS Lambda function. The function is managed using an AWS CloudFormation template. The template is configured to load the source code from an Amazon S3 bucket. The Developer manually created a .ZIP file deployment package containing the changes and put the file into the correct location on Amazon S3. When the function is invoked, the code changes have not been applied. What step is required to update the function with the changes?
o: Delete the .ZIP file on S3, and re-upload by using a different object key name.
Update the CloudFormation stack with the correct values for the function code properties S3Bucket, S3Key, or S3ObjectVersion.
Ensure that the function source code is base64-encoded before uploading the deployment package to S3.
Modify the execution role of the Lambda function to allow S3 access permission to the deployment package .ZIP file.
questions.e: Lambda created by CloudFormation only changes when the stack is updated. If the S3 key and bucket stay the same, CloudFormation sees no change, so the Developer must update the stack with a changed S3Bucket, S3Key or S3ObjectVersion value to trigger the code update.
