Base64 encoding and execution role permissions are not the problem. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer wants to enable AWS X-Ray for a secure application that runs in an Amazon ECS environment. What combination of steps will enable X-Ray? (Select THREE)
o: Create a Docker image that runs the X-Ray daemon.
Add instrumentation to the application code for X-Ray.
Install the X-Ray daemon on the underlying EC2 instance.
Configure and use an IAM EC2 instance role.
Register the application with X-Ray.
Configure and use an IAM role for tasks.
questions.e: On ECS, run the X-Ray daemon as a sidecar container from a Docker image, instrument the application with the X-Ray SDK, and give the task an IAM task role permitting the daemon to send data to X-Ray. Installing the daemon on the EC2 instance or using the instance role is less appropriate for containers, and there is no step to register the application. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is designing a new application that uses Amazon S3. To satisfy compliance requirements, the Developer must encrypt the data at rest. How can the Developer accomplish this?
o: Use s3:x-amz-acl as a condition in the S3 bucket policy.
Use Amazon RDS with default encryption.
Use aws:SecureTransport as a condition in the S3 bucket policy.
Turn on S3 default encryption for the S3 bucket.
questions.e: Turning on S3 default encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) for the bucket encrypts all new objects at rest. The ACL condition and SecureTransport condition address access control and encryption in transit, and RDS is a different service. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An AWS Elastic Beanstalk application needs to be deployed in multiple regions and requires a different Amazon Machine Image (AMI) in each region. Which AWS CloudFormation template key can be used to specify the correct AMI for each region?
o: Parameters.
Outputs.
Mappings.
Resources.
questions.e: The Mappings section of a CloudFormation template holds static lookup tables, such as a Region to AMI ID map, which can be read with Fn::FindInMap using the AWS::Region pseudo parameter. Parameters need user input, Outputs export values, and Resources define resources. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer wants to find a list of items in a global secondary index from an Amazon DynamoDB table. Which DynamoDB API call can the Developer use in order to consume the LEAST number of read capacity units?
o: Scan operation using eventually-consistent reads.
Query operation using strongly-consistent reads.
Query operation using eventually-consistent reads.
Scan operation using strongly-consistent reads.
questions.e: Query is more efficient than Scan because it reads only items matching a key condition, and eventually consistent reads cost half the read capacity of strongly consistent reads. Strongly consistent reads are also not supported on global secondary indexes. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has published an update to an application that is served to a global user base using Amazon CloudFront. After deploying the application, users are not able to see the updated changes. How can the Developer resolve this issue?
o: Remove the origin from the CloudFront configuration and add it again.
Disable forwarding of query strings and request headers from the CloudFront distribution configuration.
Invalidate all the application objects from the edge caches.
Disable the CloudFront distribution and enable it again to update all the edge locations.
questions.e: CloudFront serves cached copies until they expire, so to see updates immediately, invalidate the cached objects at the edge locations (or use versioned file names). Removing the origin, disabling the distribution or changing forwarding settings does not clear cached objects. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer must deploy a new AWS Lambda function using an AWS CloudFormation template. Which procedures will deploy a Lambda function? (Select TWO)
o: Upload the code to an AWS CodeCommit repository, then add a reference to it in an AWS::Lambda::Function resource in the template.
Create an AWS::Lambda::Function resource in the template, then write the code directly inside the CloudFormation template.
Upload a .ZIP file containing the function code to Amazon S3, then add a reference to it in an AWS::Lambda::Function resource in the template.
Upload a .ZIP file to AWS CloudFormation containing the function code, then add a reference to it in an AWS::Lambda::Function resource in the template.
Upload the function code to a private Git repository, then add a reference to it in an AWS::Lambda::Function resource in the template.
questions.e: A Lambda function in CloudFormation can include code inline with the ZipFile property (for small code, in some runtimes) or reference a ZIP in S3 with S3Bucket and S3Key. CloudFormation cannot pull code directly from CodeCommit, from a ZIP uploaded to CloudFormation itself, or from a private Git repository. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: How should custom libraries be utilized in AWS Lambda?
o: Host the library on Amazon S3 and reference to it from the Lambda function.
Install the library locally and upload a ZIP file of the Lambda function.
Import the necessary Lambda blueprint when creating the function.
Modify the function runtime to include the necessary library.
questions.e: Custom libraries must be included in the deployment package, so install them locally next to the function code and upload everything as a ZIP (or use layers). Lambda cannot reference libraries hosted on S3 at runtime, blueprints are templates, and the runtime cannot be modified. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company needs to secure its existing website running behind an Elastic Load Balancer. The website's Amazon EC2 instances are CPU-constrained. What should be done to secure the website while not increasing the CPU load on the EC2 web servers? (Select TWO)
o: Configure an Elastic Load Balancer with SSL pass-through.
Configure SSL certificates on an Elastic Load Balancer.
Configure an Elastic Load Balancer with a Loadable Storage System.
Install SSL certificates on the EC2 instances.
Configure an Elastic Load Balancer with SSL termination.
questions.e: Offloading TLS to the load balancer removes the encryption work from the CPU-constrained instances. Install the SSL certificate on the ELB and terminate SSL there, then talk to instances over HTTP. SSL pass-through and installing certificates on the EC2 instances keep the encryption load on the instances. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is writing an imaging micro service on AWS Lambda. The service is dependent on several libraries that are not available in the Lambda runtime environment. Which strategy should the Developer follow to create the Lambda deployment package?
o: Create a ZIP file with the source code and all dependent libraries.
Create a ZIP file with the source code and a script that installs the dependent libraries at runtime.
Create a ZIP file with the source code. Stage the dependent libraries on an Amazon S3 bucket indicated by the Lambda environment variable LD_LIBRARY_PATH.
Create a ZIP file with the source code and a buildspec.yaml file that installs the dependent libraries on AWS Lambda.
questions.e: A Lambda deployment package must contain the function code plus all libraries not in the runtime, bundled in a ZIP. Lambda cannot install libraries at runtime from scripts, buildspec files are for CodeBuild, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH does not point to S3. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is designing a fault-tolerant environment where client sessions will be saved. How can the Developer ensure that no sessions are lost if an Amazon EC2 instance fails?
o: Use sticky sessions with an Elastic Load Balancer target group.
Use Amazon SQS to save session data.
Use Amazon DynamoDB to perform scalable session handling.
Use Elastic Load Balancer connection draining to stop sending requests to failing instances.
questions.e: Storing sessions in DynamoDB keeps session data outside the instances, in a highly available, scalable store, so a failed instance does not lose any sessions. Sticky sessions keep data on the instance, SQS is not a session store, and connection draining only helps to finish in-flight requests when removing instances. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: In a move toward using microservices, a company's Management team has asked all Development teams to build their services so that API requests depend only on that service's data store. One team is building a Payments service which has its own database; the service needs data that originates in the Accounts database. Both are using Amazon DynamoDB. What approach will result in the simplest, decoupled, and reliable method to get near-real time updates from the Accounts database?
o: Use Amazon Glue to perform frequent ETL updates from the Accounts database to the Payments database.
Use Amazon ElastiCache in Payments, with the cache updated by triggers in the Accounts database.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver all changes from the Accounts database to the Payments database.
Use Amazon DynamoDB Streams to deliver all changes from the Accounts database to the Payments database.
questions.e: DynamoDB Streams captures item changes in the Accounts table in near real time, and a consumer (such as Lambda) can apply them to the Payments data store, giving a simple, decoupled and reliable approach. Glue ETL is batch, ElastiCache triggers do not exist, and Firehose is intended for delivering data to destinations like S3 and not for DynamoDB-to-DynamoDB synchronization. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company needs a fully-managed source control service that will work in AWS. The service must ensure that revision control synchronizes multiple distributed repositories by exchanging sets of changes peer-to-peer. All users need to work productively even when not connected to a network. Which source control service should be used?
o: Subversion.
AWS CodeBuild.
AWS CodeCommit.
AWS CodeStar.
questions.e: AWS CodeCommit is a managed Git service. Git is a distributed version control system where each user has a full local repository, can work offline, and changes are exchanged peer-to-peer. Subversion is centralized, CodeBuild is a build service and CodeStar is a project tool, not a repository. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is writing a serverless application that requires that an AWS Lambda function be invoked every 10 minutes. What is an automated and serverless way to trigger the function?
o: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance based on Linux, and edit its /etc/crontab file by adding a command to periodically invoke the Lambda function.
Configure an environment variable named PERIOD for the Lambda function. Set the value to 600.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch Events rule that triggers on a regular schedule to invoke the Lambda function.
Create an Amazon SNS topic that has a subscription to the Lambda function with a 600-second timer.
questions.e: A CloudWatch Events (EventBridge) rule with a schedule expression such as rate(10 minutes) can invoke the Lambda function, with no servers to manage. A cron job on EC2 is not serverless, environment variables do not trigger a function, and SNS subscriptions have no timer. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is building an application to track athlete performance using an Amazon DynamoDB table. Each item in the table is identified by a partition key (user_id) and a sort key (sport_name). The table design is shown below. (Note: Not all table attributes are shown) A Developer is asked to write a leaderboard application to display the top performers (user_id) based on the score for each sport_name. What process will allow the Developer to extract results MOST efficiently from the DynamoDB table?
o: Use a DynamoDB query operation with the key attributes of user_id and sport_name and order the results based on the score attribute.
Create a global secondary index with a partition key of sport_name and a sort key of score, and get the results.
Use a DynamoDB scan operation to retrieve scores and user_id based on sport_name, and order the results based on the score attribute.
Create a local secondary index with a primary key of sport_name and a sort key of score and get the results based on the score attribute.
questions.e: A GSI with partition key sport_name and sort key score lets the Developer query all users for a sport sorted by score, to get the top performers efficiently. Querying or scanning the base table by user_id would scan everything, and a local secondary index must use the same partition key as the base table (user_id), so it cannot have sport_name as its partition key. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is creating a mobile application that will not require users to log in. What is the MOST efficient method to grant users access to AWS resources?
o: Use an identity provider to securely authenticate with the application.
Create an AWS Lambda function to create an IAM user when a user accesses the application.
Create credentials using AWS KMS and apply these credentials to users when using the application.
Use Amazon Cognito to associate unauthenticated users with an IAM role that has limited access to resources.
questions.e: Amazon Cognito identity pools support unauthenticated (guest) identities and associate them with an IAM role with limited permissions, providing temporary AWS credentials without any login. Creating IAM users or credentials per user is complex and insecure, and an identity provider requires users to authenticate. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application running on Amazon EC2 instances must access objects within an Amazon S3 bucket that are encrypted using server-side encryption using AWS KMS encryption keys (SSE-KMS). The application must have access to the customer master key (CMK) to decrypt the objects. Which combination of steps will grant the application access? (Select TWO)
o: Write an S3 bucket policy that grants the bucket access to the key.
Grant access to the key in the IAM EC2 role attached to the application's EC2 instances.
Write a key policy that enables IAM policies to grant access to the key.
Grant access to the key in the S3 bucket's ACL.
Create a Systems Manager parameter that exposes the KMS key to the EC2 instances.
questions.e: To decrypt SSE-KMS objects, the application role needs permission to use the key (kms:Decrypt), granted in the IAM policy of the EC2 instance role, and the KMS key policy must allow this, such as by enabling IAM policies to grant access to the key. Bucket policies, ACLs and Systems Manager parameters do not grant KMS key permissions. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: What does an Amazon SQS delay queue accomplish?
o: Messages are hidden for a configurable amount of time when they are first added to the queue.
Messages are hidden for a configurable amount of time after they are consumed from the queue.
The consumer can poll the queue for a configurable amount of time before retrieving a message.
Message cannot be deleted for a configurable amount of time after they are consumed from the queue.
questions.e: An SQS delay queue hides new messages from consumers for a configurable delay (0 to 15 minutes) after they are added to the queue. Hiding after consumption is the visibility timeout, polling for a period is long polling, and preventing deletion is not a feature. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has multiple Developers located across the globe who are updating code incrementally for a development project. When Developers upload code concurrently, internet connectivity is slow and it is taking a long time to upload code for deployment in AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Which step will result in minimized upload and deployment time with the LEAST amount of administrative effort?
o: Allow the Developers to upload the code to an Amazon S3 bucket, and deploy it directly to Elastic Beanstalk.
Allow the Developers to upload the code to a central FTP server to deploy the application to Elastic Beanstalk.
Create an AWS CodeCommit repository, allow the Developers to commit code to it, and then directly deploy the code to Elastic Beanstalk.
Create a code repository on an Amazon EC2 instance so that all Developers can update the code, and deploy the application from the instance to Elastic Beanstalk.
questions.e: CodeCommit is a managed Git service in AWS. Developers push only incremental changes (git sends deltas), which reduces upload time, and the code can be deployed directly to Elastic Beanstalk with low administrative effort. S3 uploads send full bundles, and FTP or EC2-hosted repositories require servers to manage. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company recently migrated its web, application and NoSQL database tiers to AWS. The company is using Auto Scaling to scale the web and application tiers. More than 95 percent of the Amazon DynamoDB requests are repeated read requests. How can the DynamoDB NoSQL tier be scaled up to cache these repeated requests?
o: Amazon EMR.
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator.
Amazon SQS.
Amazon CloudFront.
questions.e: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed in-memory cache for DynamoDB that reduces read latency to microseconds for repeated reads, with no application redesign beyond using the DAX client. EMR, SQS and CloudFront are not caches for DynamoDB reads. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Development team is working on a case management solution that allows medical claims to be processed and reviewed. Users log in to provide information related to their medical and financial situations. As part of the application, sensitive documents such as medical records, medical imaging, bank statements, and receipts are uploaded to Amazon S3. All documents must be securely transmitted and stored. All access to the documents must be recorded for auditing. What is the MOST secure approach?
o: Use S3 default encryption using Advanced Encryption Standard-256 (AES-256) on the destination bucket.
Use Amazon Cognito for authorization and authentication to ensure the security of the application and documents.
Use AWS Lambda to encrypt and decrypt objects as they are placed into the S3 bucket.
Use client-side encryption/decryption with Amazon S3 and AWS KMS.
questions.e: Client-side encryption with S3 and KMS encrypts the data before it leaves the application, so it is protected in transit and at rest, and KMS usage is logged by CloudTrail for audit. Server-side default encryption alone does not protect data before upload, Cognito handles authentication, and Lambda-based encryption is unnecessary. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has an internet-facing application that uses Web Identity Federation to obtain a temporary credential from AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS). The app then uses the token to access AWS services. Review the following response: Based on the response displayed what permissions are associated with the call from the application?
o: Permissions associated with the role AROACLKWSDQRAOEXAMPLE:app1.
Permissions associated with the default role used when the AWS service was built.
Permission associated with the IAM principal that owns the AccessKeyID ASgeIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE.
Permissions associated with the account that owns the AWS service.
questions.e: With web identity federation, the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity response contains temporary credentials, and calls signed with the returned AccessKeyId carry the permissions of the IAM principal that owns the key, which is the assumed role session. The role ID AROACLKWSDQRAOEXAMPLE is just an identifier in the response, and the other options are unrelated to the credentials. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is using AWS CLI, but when running list commands on a large number of resources, it is timing out. What can be done to avoid this time-out?
o: Use pagination.
Use shorthand syntax.
Use parameter values.
Use quoting strings.
questions.e: The AWS CLI by default pages results, but listing large numbers of resources in one call can time out. Using pagination with smaller page sizes (for example, --page-size) makes multiple smaller API calls and avoids timeouts. Shorthand syntax, parameter values and quoting strings only affect how commands are written. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Where can PortMapping be defined when launching containers in Amazon ECS?
o: Security groups.
Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amzon ECR).
Container agent.
Task definition.
questions.e: Port mappings, which map container ports to host ports, are defined in the container definition section of an ECS task definition. Security groups, ECR and the container agent do not define port mappings. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An organization is storing large files in Amazon S3, and is writing a web application to display meta-data about the files to end-users. Based on the metadata a user selects an object to download. The organization needs a mechanism to index the files and provide single-digit millisecond latency retrieval for the metadata. What AWS service should be used to accomplish this?
o: Amazon DynamoDB.
Amazon EC2.
AWS Lambda.
Amazon RDS.
questions.e: DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond latency, which makes it a good index for S3 object metadata that a web application queries. EC2 and Lambda are compute, and RDS is a relational database that does not provide the same latency characteristics at scale. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: While developing an application that runs on Amazon EC2 in an Amazon VPC, a Developer identifies the need for centralized storage of application-level logs. Which AWS service can be used to securely store these logs?
o: Amazon EC2 VPC Flow Logs.
Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Amazon CloudSearch.
AWS CloudTrail
questions.e: CloudWatch Logs is the managed service for centralizing and securely storing application and system logs from EC2, with retention and encryption options. VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic, CloudSearch is a search service, and CloudTrail records API calls. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A stock market monitoring application uses Amazon Kinesis for data ingestion. During simulated tests of peak data rates, the Kinesis stream cannot keep up with the incoming data. What step will allow Kinesis to accommodate the traffic during peak hours?
o: Install the Kinesis Producer Library (KPL) for ingesting data into the stream.
Reduce the data retention period to allow for more data ingestion using DecreaseStreamRetentionPeriod.
Increase the shard count of the stream using UpdateShardCount.
Ingest multiple records into the stream in a single call using PutRecords.
questions.e: When a Kinesis stream cannot keep up, throughput is limited by the number of shards, each supporting 1 MB or 1000 records per second for writes. Increasing the shard count with UpdateShardCount adds capacity. KPL and PutRecords improve producer efficiency but do not add capacity, and reducing retention does not increase ingestion. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company has an AWS CloudFormation template that is stored as a single file. The template is able to launch and create a full infrastructure stack. Which best practice would increase the maintainability of the template?
o: Use nested stacks for common template patterns.
Embed credentials to prevent typos.
Remove mappings to decrease the number of variables.
Use AWS::Include to reference publicly-hosted template files.
questions.e: Nested stacks let you reuse common template patterns, such as a load balancer or security group configuration, as separate templates, breaking a large template into manageable pieces. Embedding credentials is insecure, removing mappings does not help maintainability, and AWS::Include is a macro-based snippet include, not the best practice for this. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An on-premises application makes repeated calls to store files to Amazon S3. As usage of the application has increased, LimitExceeded errors are being logged. What should be changed to fix this error?
o: Implement exponential backoffs in the application.
Load balance the application to multiple servers.
Move the application to Amazon EC2.
Add a one second delay to each API call.
questions.e: Throttling or limit errors from AWS APIs should be handled by retrying with exponential backoff, so the application slows its request rate and retries successfully. Load balancing the app, moving it to EC2, or adding a fixed one second delay does not address bursts adaptively. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company caches session information for a web application in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants an automated way to delete old items from the table. What is the simplest way to do this?
o: Write a script that deletes old records; schedule the scripts as a cron job on an Amazon EC2 instance.
Add an attribute with the expiration time; enable the Time To Live feature based on that attribute.
Each day, create a new table to hold session data; delete the previous day's table.
Add an attribute with the expiration time; name the attribute ItemExpiration.
questions.e: DynamoDB Time To Live deletes expired items automatically at no cost. Store an expiration timestamp in an attribute and enable TTL on that attribute. Cron jobs or daily tables need extra work, and just naming an attribute ItemExpiration does nothing without enabling TTL. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application is expected to process many files. Each file takes four minutes to process each AWS Lambda invocation. The Lambda function does not return any important data. What is the fastest way to process all the files?
o: First split the files to make them smaller, then process with synchronous RequestResponse Lambda invocations.
Make synchronous RequestResponse Lambda invocations and process the files one by one.
Make asynchronous Event Lambda invocations and process the files in parallel.
First join all the files, then process it all at once with an asynchronous Event Lambda invocation.
questions.e: Asynchronous Event invocations return immediately and let you run many invocations in parallel, so the files are processed concurrently and fastest, and there is no need for a response. Synchronous one-by-one processing is slow, and joining files makes the single invocation exceed run time and be slower. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: The upload of a 15 GB object to Amazon S3 fails. The error message reads: Your proposed upload exceeds the maximum allowed object size.. What technique will allow the Developer to upload this object?
o: Upload the object using the multi-part upload API.
Upload the object over an AWS Direct Connect connection.
Contact AWS Support to increase the object size limit.
Upload the object to another AWS region.
questions.e: A single PUT upload to S3 is limited to 5 GB, while objects can be up to 5 TB. Use the multipart upload API to upload larger objects in parts. Direct Connect, another region or support requests do not change the single-upload limit. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: AWS CodeBuild builds code for an application, creates the Docker image, pushes the image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR), and tags the image with a unique identifier. If the Developers already have AWS CLI configured on their workstations, how can the Docker images be pulled to the workstations?
o: Run the following: docker pull REPOSITORY URI : TAG.
Run the output of the following: aws ecr get-login and then run: docker pull REPOSITORY URI : TAG.
Run the following: aws ecr get-login and then run: docker pull REPOSITORY URI : TAG.
Run the output of the following: aws ecr get-download-url-for-layer and then run: docker pull REPOSITORY URI : TAG.
questions.e: Note: the marked answer may be wrong. Docker must authenticate to ECR before pulling, and the marked option (run the output of aws ecr get-login, then docker pull) was correct for AWS CLI v1, but get-login was removed in CLI v2, where you run aws ecr get-login-password piped to docker login and then docker pull. Running docker pull without logging in fails, and get-download-url-for-layer does not produce a login command. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A web application is designed to allow new users to create accounts using their email addresses. The application will store attributes for each user, and is expecting millions of user to sign up. What should the Developer implement to achieve the design goals?
o: Amazon Cognito user pools.
AWS Mobile Hub user data storage.
Amazon Cognito Sync.
AWS Mobile Hub cloud logic.
questions.e: Amazon Cognito user pools are a scalable user directory supporting sign-up and sign-in with email addresses, and can store user attributes for millions of users. Cognito Sync stores data per identity for syncing and Mobile Hub options are not user directories. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company needs a new REST API that can return information about the contents of an Amazon S3 bucket, such as a count of the objects stored in it. The company has decided that the new API should be written as a microservice using AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway. How should the Developer ensure that the microservice has the necessary access to the Amazon S3 bucket, while adhering to security best practices?
o: Create an IAM user that has permissions to access the Amazon S3 bucket, and store the IAM user credentials in the Lambda function source code.
Create an IAM role that has permissions to access the Amazon S3 bucket and assign it to the Lambda function as its execution role.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket policy that specifies the Lambda service as its principal and assign it to the Amazon S3 bucket.
Create an IAM role, attach the AmazonS3FullAccess managed policy to it, and assign the role to the Lambda function as its execution role.
questions.e: The secure approach is to create an IAM role with permissions to the specific S3 bucket and attach it as the Lambda execution role, so the function receives temporary credentials. Embedding IAM user credentials is insecure, a bucket policy alone does not cover it, and AmazonS3FullAccess violates least privilege. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An organization is using Amazon CloudFront to ensure that its users experience low-latency access to its web application. The organization has identified a need to encrypt all traffic between users and CloudFront, and all traffic between CloudFront and the web application. How can these requirements be met? (Choose TWO)
o: Use AWS KMS to encrypt traffic between CloudFront and the web application.
Set the Origin Protocol Policy to HTTPS Only.
Set the Origin's HTTP Port to 443.
Set the Viewer Protocol Policy to HTTPS Only or Redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Enable the CloudFront option Restrict Viewer Access.
questions.e: Encrypting both legs requires setting the Viewer Protocol Policy to HTTPS Only or Redirect HTTP to HTTPS for traffic between users and CloudFront, and Origin Protocol Policy to HTTPS Only for traffic between CloudFront and the origin. KMS does not encrypt traffic, port 443 alone does not enable HTTPS, and Restrict Viewer Access controls signed URL access. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application is using Amazon DynamoDB as its data store, and should be able to read 100 items per second as strongly consistent reads. Each item is 5 KB in size. To what value should the table's provisioned read throughput be set?
o: 50 read capacity units.
100 read capacity units.
200 read capacity units.
500 read capacity units.
questions.e: A strongly consistent read of up to 4 KB uses 1 RCU, so a 5 KB item rounds up to 2 RCUs. At 100 reads per second, that is 200 RCUs. 50 would be eventually consistent for 4 KB items, and the other values do not match the calculation. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application uses Lambda functions to extract metadata from files uploaded to an S3 bucket; the metadata is stored in Amazon DynamoDB. The application starts behaving unexpectedly, and the Developer wants to examine the logs of the Lambda function code for errors. Based on this system configuration, where would the Developer find the logs?
o: Amazon S3.
AWS CloudTrail.
Amazon CloudWatch.
Amazon DynamoDB
questions.e: Lambda automatically sends function logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, in a log group named after the function. S3 and DynamoDB store the data, and CloudTrail records API calls and not function output. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer is creating a Lambda function that will generate and export a file. The function requires 100 MB of temporary storage for temporary files while executing. These files will not be needed after the function is complete. How can the Developer MOST efficiently handle the temporary files?
o: Store the files in EBS and delete the files at the end of the Lambda function.
Copy the files to EFS and delete the files at the end of the Lambda function.
Store the files in the /tmp directory and delete the files at the end of the Lambda function.
Copy the files to an S3 bucket with a lifecycle policy to delete the files.
questions.e: Lambda provides ephemeral storage in the /tmp directory (512 MB by default), which is local, fast and cheap, ideal for 100 MB of temporary files. EBS cannot be attached to Lambda, and EFS or S3 add unnecessary complexity and cost for temporary files. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has developed a web application and wants to deploy it quickly on a Tomcat server on AWS. The Developer wants to avoid having to manage the underlying infrastructure. What is the easiest way to deploy the application, based on these requirements?
o: AWS CloudFormation.
AWS Elastic Beanstalk.
Amazon S3.
AWS CodePipeline
questions.e: Elastic Beanstalk supports Tomcat and manages provisioning, load balancing, scaling and monitoring, so the Developer just uploads the application. CloudFormation requires defining infrastructure, S3 stores files, and CodePipeline is for release automation. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application runs on multiple EC2 instances behind an ELB. Where is the session data best written so that it can be served reliably across multiple requests?
o: Write data to Amazon ElastiCache.
Write data to Amazon Elastic Block Store.
Write data to Amazon EC2 Instance Store.
Write data to the root filesystem.
questions.e: Sessions should be stored outside the instances in a shared in-memory store like ElastiCache so any instance behind the ELB can read them. EBS, instance store and the root filesystem are local to a single instance and cannot be shared between instances reliably. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is migrating from a monolithic architecture to a microservices-based architecture. The Developers need to refactor the application so that the many microservices can asynchronously communicate with each other without impacting performance. Use of which managed AWS services will enable asynchronous message passing? (Choose TWO)
o: Amazon SQS.
Amazon Cognito.
Amazon Kinesis.
Amazon SNS.
Amazon ElastiCache.
questions.e: SQS (queue) and SNS (pub/sub) are managed messaging services for asynchronous communication between microservices, decoupling producers and consumers. Cognito is for identity, Kinesis is for streaming data analytics, and ElastiCache is a cache. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: According to best practice, how should access keys be managed in AWS? (Choose TWO)
o: Use the same access key in all applications for consistency.
Delete all access keys for the account root user.
Leave unused access keys in the account for tracking purposes.
Embed and encrypt access keys in code for continuous deployment.
Use Amazon IAM roles instead of access keys where possible.
questions.e: Best practices are to delete the root user access keys (not to use root keys at all) and to use IAM roles with temporary credentials instead of long-term access keys. Sharing keys, keeping unused keys, or embedding keys in code, even encrypted, are poor security practices. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application running on an Amazon Linux EC2 instance needs to manage the AWS infrastructure. How can the EC2 instance be configured to make AWS API calls securely?
o: Sign the AWS CLI command using the signature version 4 process.
Run the aws configure AWS CLI command and specify the access key id and secret access key.
Specify a role for the EC2 instance with the necessary privileges.
Pass the access key id and secret access key as parameters for each AWS CLI command.
questions.e: Attach an IAM role through an instance profile to the EC2 instance, and the CLI or SDK automatically picks up temporary credentials from the instance metadata. Configuring or passing access keys, or signing manually, means storing long-term credentials, which is insecure. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application needs to use the IP address of the client in its processing. The application has been moved into AWS and has been placed behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). However, all the client IP addresses now appear to be the same. The application must maintain the ability to scale horizontally. Based on this scenario, what is the MOST cost-effective solution to this problem?
o: Remove the application from the ALB. Delete the ALB and change Amazon Route 53 to direct traffic to the instance running the application.
Remove the application from the ALB. Create a Classic Load Balancer in its place. Direct traffic to the application using the HTTP protocol.
Alter the application code to inspect the X-Forwarded-For header. Ensure that the code can work properly if a list of IP addresses is passed in the header.
Alter the application code to inspect a custom header. Alter the client code to pass the IP address in the custom header.
questions.e: Behind an ALB, the source IP seen by the application is the load balancer's. The ALB adds the original client IP in the X-Forwarded-For header, which may contain a list of addresses, so changing the code to read it is the cheapest solution that keeps horizontal scaling. Removing the load balancer breaks scaling, Classic LB with HTTP would also need the header unless using proxy protocol, and a custom header would require client changes. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A development team is using AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy a two-tier application that consists of a load-balanced web tier and an Amazon RDS database tier in production. The team would like to separate the RDS instance from the Elastic Beanstalk. How can this be accomplished?
o: Use the Elastic Beanstalk CLI to disassociate the database.
Use the AWS CLI to disassociate the database.
Change the deployment policy to disassociate the database.
Recreate a new Elastic Beanstalk environment without Amazon RDS.
questions.e: In Elastic Beanstalk, a database created as part of an environment is tied to the environment lifecycle and cannot be detached later. To separate it, create a new environment without RDS (connecting to an externally created database) and migrate. CLI commands or deployment policies cannot disassociate the database. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is using AWS CodePipeline to deliver one of its applications. The delivery pipeline is triggered by changes to the master branch of an AWS CodeCommit repository and uses AWS CodeBuild to implement the test and build stages of the process and AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the application. The pipeline has been operating successfully for several months and there have been no modifications. Following a recent change to the application's source code, AWS CodeDeploy has not deployed the updates application as expected. What are the possible causes? (Choose TWO)
o: The change was not made in the master branch of the AWS CodeCommit repository.
One of the earlier stages in the pipeline failed and the pipeline has terminated.
One of the Amazon EC2 instances in the company's AWS CodePipeline cluster is inactive.
The AWS CodePipeline is incorrectly configured and is not executing AWS CodeDeploy.
AWS CodePipeline does not have permissions to access AWS CodeCommit.
questions.e: A pipeline only triggers on changes to the configured branch (master), so a commit on another branch will not start it, and if an earlier stage such as build or test fails, the pipeline stops before reaching the deploy stage. The pipeline worked for months, so misconfiguration or permissions are unlikely, and CodePipeline has no EC2 cluster. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A social media company is using Amazon Cognito in order to synchronize profiles across different mobile devices, to enable end users to have a seamless experience. Which of the following configurations can be used to silently notify users whenever an update is available on all other devices?
o: Modify the user pool to include all the devices which keep them in sync.
Use the SyncCallback interface to receive notifications on the application.
Use an Amazon Cognito stream to analyze the data and push the notifications.
Use the push synchronization feature with the appropriate IAM role.
questions.e: Cognito Sync supports push synchronization, which uses SNS and an IAM role to send silent push notifications to all of a user's devices when the data changes. SyncCallback handles events within the app but does not push to other devices, user pools do not track devices, and streams are for analysis. Cognito Sync is now superseded by AppSync. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An on-premises application is implemented using a Linux, Apache, MySQL and PHP (LAMP) stack. The Developer wants to run this application in AWS. Which of the following sets of AWS services can be used to run this stack?
o: Amazon API Gateway, Amazon S3.
AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB.
Amazon EC2, Amazon Aurora.
Amazon Cognito, Amazon RDS.
Amazon ECS, Amazon EBS.
questions.e: A LAMP stack runs on Linux servers with Apache and PHP, which map to EC2, and MySQL, which maps to Amazon Aurora (MySQL-compatible). Lambda with DynamoDB, API Gateway with S3, and the others do not support running Apache and PHP with MySQL as is. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An application displays a status dashboard. The status is updated by 1 KB messages from an SQS queue. Although the status changes infrequently, the Developer must minimize the time between the message arrival in the queue and the dashboard update. What technique provides the shortest delay in updating the dashboard?
o: Retrieve the messages from the queue using long polling every 20 seconds.
Reduce the size of the messages by compressing them before sending.
Retrieve the messages from the queue using short polling every 10 seconds.
Reduce the size of each message payload by sending it in two parts.
questions.e: Long polling with a 20 second wait lets the consumer receive messages as soon as they arrive, and queries all servers, so it returns with minimum delay and avoids empty responses. Short polling every 10 seconds can add delay and may miss messages on some servers, and message size changes do not materially affect delay. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An on-premises legacy application is caching data files locally and writing shared images to local disks. What is necessary to allow for horizontal scaling when migrating the application to AWS?
o: Modify the application to have both shared images and caching data written to Amazon EBS.
Modify the application to read and write cache data on Amazon S3, and also store shared images on S3.
Modify the application to use Amazon S3 for serving shared images; cache data can then be written to local disks.
Modify the application to read and write cache data on Amazon S3, while continuing to write shared images to local disks.
questions.e: To scale horizontally, instances must be stateless, so shared images and cached data must be stored in a shared service like S3. EBS volumes attach to one instance, and keeping anything on local disks makes instances differ and not share data. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer must trigger an AWS Lambda function based on the item lifecycle activity in an Amazon DynamoDB table. How can the Developer create the solution?
o: Enable a DynamoDB stream that publishes an Amazon SNS message. Trigger the Lambda function synchronously from the SNS message.
Enable a DynamoDB stream that publishes an SNS message. Trigger the Lambda function asynchronously from the SNS message.
Enable a DynamoDB stream, and trigger the Lambda function synchronously from the stream.
Enable a DynamoDB stream, and trigger the Lambda function asynchronously from the stream.
questions.e: Note: the marked answer may be wrong. A Lambda function is triggered from a DynamoDB stream through an event source mapping, where Lambda polls the stream and invokes the function synchronously, so the synchronous stream trigger option is likely correct. Streams cannot publish to SNS directly, so the SNS options are wrong, and stream-based invocations are not asynchronous. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: After installing the AWS CLI, a Developer tries to run the command aws configure but receives the following error: Error: aws: command not found. What is the most likely cause of this error?
o: The aws executable is not in the PATH environment variable.
Access to the aws executable has been denied to the installer.
Incorrect AWS credentials were provided.
The aws script does not have an executable file mode.
questions.e: The error command not found means the shell cannot find the aws executable, usually because its install location is not in the PATH environment variable. Credentials errors would appear after the command runs, and permission denial would show a different message. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: The Developer for a retail company must integrate a fraud detection solution into the order processing solution. The fraud detection solution takes between ten and thirty minutes to verify an order. At peak, the web site can receive one hundred orders per minute. What is the most scalable method to add the fraud detection solution to the order processing pipeline?
o: Add all new orders to an Amazon SQS queue. Configure a fleet of 10 EC2 instances spanning multiple AZs with the fraud detection solution installed on them to pull orders from this queue. Update the order with a pass or fails status.

Add all new orders to an SQS queue. Configure an Auto Scaling group that uses the queue depth metric as its unit of scale to launch a dynamically-sized fleet of EC2 instances spanning multiple AZs with the fraud detection solution installed on them to pull orders from this queue. Update the order with a pass or fails status.

Add all new orders to an Amazon Kinesis Stream. Subscribe a Lambda function to automatically read batches of records from the Kinesis Stream. The Lambda function includes the fraud detection software and will update the order with a pass or fail status.

Write all new orders to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure DynamoDB Streams to include all new orders. Subscribe a Lambda function to automatically read batches of records from the Kinesis Stream. The Lambda function includes the fraud detection software and will update the order with a pass or fail status.
questions.e: SQS decouples order intake from the slow 10 to 30 minute processing, and an Auto Scaling group scaled on queue depth adjusts the fleet to the load, which is most scalable. A fixed fleet of 10 cannot handle 100 orders per minute, and Lambda has a 15 minute maximum run time so it cannot run a 30 minute check. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: When a Developer tries to run an AWS CodeBuild project, it raises an error because the length of all environment variables exceeds the limit for the combined maximum of characters. What is the recommended solution?
o: Add the export LC_ALL="en_US.utf8" command to the pre_build section to ensure POSIX localization.
Use Amazon Cognito to store key-value pairs for large numbers of environment variables.
Update the settings for the build project to use an Amazon S3 bucket for large numbers of environment variables.
Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store large numbers of environment variables.
questions.e: When CodeBuild environment variables exceed the size limit, store them in Systems Manager Parameter Store and have the project reference them as parameter-store variables. Cognito is not a key-value store for this, S3 is not a supported source of environment variables, and the locale export does not affect limits. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A set of APIs are exposed to customers using the Amazon API Gateway. These APIs have caching enabled on the API Gateway. Customers have asked for an option to invalidate this cache for each of the APIs. What action can be taken to allow API customers to invalidate the API Cache?
o: Ask customers to use AWS credentials to call the InvalidateCache API.
Ask customers to invoke an AWS API endpoint which invalidates the cache.
Ask customers to pass an HTTP header called Cache-Control:max-age=0.
Ask customers to add a query string parameter called INVALIDATE_CACHE when making an API call.
questions.e: API Gateway lets clients invalidate a cache entry by sending a Cache-Control: max-age=0 header, if the caller is authorized (or if the setting does not require authorization). This does not require customers to use AWS credentials or special endpoints. A query string called INVALIDATE_CACHE is not a feature. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has been asked to build a real-time dashboard web application to visualize the key prefixes and storage size of objects in Amazon S3 buckets. Amazon DynamoDB will be used to store the Amazon S3 metadata. What is the optimal and MOST cost-effective design to ensure that the real-time dashboard is kept up to date with the state of the objects in the Amazon S3 buckets?
o: Use an Amazon CloudWatch event backed by an AWS Lambda function. Issue an Amazon S3 API call to get a list of all Amazon S3 objects and persist the metadata within DynamoDB. Have the web application poll the DynamoDB table to reflect this change.
Use Amazon S3 Event Notification backed by a Lambda function to persist the metadata into DynamoDB. Have the web application poll the DynamoDB table to reflect this change.
Run a cron job within an Amazon EC2 instance to list all objects within Amazon S3 and persist the metadata into DynamoDB. Have the web application poll the DynamoDB table to reflect this change.
Create a new Amazon EMR cluster to get all the metadata about Amazon S3 objects; persist the metadata into DynamoDB. Have the web application poll the DynamoDB table to reflect this change.
questions.e: S3 Event Notifications trigger a Lambda function when objects are created or deleted, which writes metadata to DynamoDB, keeping the dashboard up to date in near real time and cheaply, with no polling of S3. Listing all objects on a schedule, cron jobs or EMR are costly and not real time. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer must repeatedly and consistently deploy a serverless RESTful API on AWS. Which techniques will work? (Choose TWO)
o: Define a Swagger file. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy the Swagger file.
Define a Swagger file. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the Swagger file.
Deploy a SAM template with an inline Swagger definition.
Define a Swagger file. Deploy a SAM template that references the Swagger file.
Define an inline Swagger definition in a Lambda function. Invoke the Lambda function.
questions.e: To deploy a serverless REST API consistently, use a SAM template, with either an inline Swagger/OpenAPI definition or a reference to a Swagger file in the DefinitionBody or DefinitionUri property. Elastic Beanstalk and CodeDeploy do not deploy Swagger files as API Gateway APIs, and a Lambda function cannot create an API from Swagger by being invoked. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: An existing serverless application processes uploaded image files. The process currently uses a single Lambda function that takes an image file, performs the processing, and stores the file in Amazon S3. Users of the application now require thumbnail generation of the images. Users want to avoid any impact to the time it takes to perform the image uploads. How can thumbnail generation be added to the application, meeting user requirements while minimizing changes to existing code?
o: Change the existing Lambda function handling the uploads to create thumbnails at the time of upload. Have the function store both the image and thumbnail in Amazon S3.
Create a second Lambda function that handles thumbnail generation and storage. Change the existing Lambda function to invoke it asynchronously.
Create an S3 event notification with a Lambda function destination. Create a new Lambda function to generate and store thumbnails.
Create an S3 event notification to an SQS Queue. Create a scheduled Lambda function that processes the queue, and generates and stores thumbnails.
questions.e: An S3 event notification with a Lambda destination triggers a new thumbnail function asynchronously after upload, so upload times are unaffected and the existing code is untouched. Changing the existing function slows uploads, invoking another function from it modifies existing code, and a scheduled SQS processor adds delay and complexity. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company is using Amazon API Gateway to manage access to a set of microservices implemented as AWS Lambda functions. Following a bug report, the company makes a minor breaking change to one of the APIs. In order to avoid impacting existing clients when the new API is deployed, the company wants to allow clients six months to migrate from v1 to v2. Which approach should the Developer use to handle this change?
o: Update the underlying Lambda function and provide clients with the new Lambda invocation URL.
Use API Gateway to automatically propagate the change to clients, specifying 180 days in the phased deployment parameter.
Use API Gateway to deploy a new stage named v2 to the API and provide users with its URL.
Update the underlying Lambda function, create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the updated Lambda function as its origin.
questions.e: API Gateway stages let you deploy different versions of the API side by side, so a new v2 stage with its own URL lets clients migrate over six months while v1 keeps working. Changing the Lambda function breaks existing clients, and there is no phased deployment parameter that works this way. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A company developed a set of APIs that are being served through the Amazon API Gateway. The API calls need to be authenticated based on OpenID identity providers such as Amazon or Facebook. The APIs should allow access based on a custom authorization model. Which is the simplest and MOST secure design to use to build an authentication and authorization model for the APIs?
o: Use Amazon Cognito user pools and a custom authorizer to authenticate and authorize users based on JSON Web Tokens.
Build a OpenID token broker with Amazon and Facebook. Users will authenticate with these identify providers and pass the JSON Web Token to the API to authenticate each API call.

Store user credentials in Amazon DynamoDB and have the application retrieve temporary credentials from AWS STS. Make API calls by passing user credentials to the APIs for authentication and authorization.
Use Amazon RDS to store user credentials and pass them to the APIs for authentications and authorization.
questions.e: Cognito user pools can federate with identity providers like Amazon and Facebook and issue JSON Web Tokens, and an API Gateway Lambda authorizer can apply custom authorization logic on the tokens. Building a custom token broker or storing credentials in DynamoDB or RDS is more complex and less secure. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Where should an Elastic Beanstalk configuration file named healthcheckur1.config be placed in the application source bundle?
o: In the root of the application.
In the bin folder.
In healthcheckur1.config.ebextension under root.
In the .ebextensions folder.
questions.e: Elastic Beanstalk reads configuration files from a folder named .ebextensions in the root of the application source bundle, and files must end in .config. The root, a bin folder or a custom extension folder are not read. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A Developer has implemented a Lambda function that needs to add new customers to an RDS database that is expected to run hundreds of times per hour. The Lambda function is configured to use 512MB of RAM and is based on the following pseudo code. After testing the Lambda function, the Developer notices that the Lambda execution time is much longer than expected. What should the Developer do to improve performance?
o: Increase the amount of RAM allocated to the Lambda function, which will increase the number of threads the Lambda can use.
Increase the size of the RDS database to allow for an increased number of database connections each hour.
Move the database connection and close statement out of the handler. Place the connection in the global space.
Replace RDS wit Amazon DynamoDB to implement control over the number of writes per second.
questions.e: In Lambda, code outside the handler runs once per execution environment and is reused between invocations. Creating the database connection in global scope means it is reused instead of opened and closed on every invocation, reducing execution time. More RAM, a bigger RDS instance or DynamoDB do not address connection setup overhead. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: A static website is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket. Several HTML pages on the site use JavaScript to download images from another Amazon S3 bucket. These images are not displayed when users browse the site. What is the possible cause for the issue?
o: The referenced Amazon S3 bucket is in another region.
The images must be stored in the same Amazon S3 bucket.
Port 80 must be opened on the security group in which the Amazon S3 bucket is located.
Cross Origin Resource Sharing must be enabled on the Amazon S3 bucket.
questions.e: Browsers block cross-origin requests made by JavaScript from a page on one origin to a different origin unless the target allows it. Enable Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) on the bucket holding the images and allow the website origin. Region differences, security groups (S3 has none) and same-bucket restrictions are not relevant. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)

questions.q: Amazon S3 has the following structure: S3://BUCKET/FOLDERNAME/FILENAME.zip. Which S3 best practice would optimize performance with thousands of PUT request each second to a single bucket?
o: Prefix folder names with user id; for example, s3://BUCKET/2013-FOLDERNAME/FILENAME.zip.
Prefix file names with timestamps; for example, s3://BUCKET/FOLDERNAME/2013-26-05-15-00-00-FILENAME.zip.
Prefix file names with random hex hashes; for example, s3://BUCKET/FOLDERNAME/23a6-FILENAME.zip.
Prefix folder names with random hex hashes; for example, s3://BUCKET/23a6-FOLDERNAME/FILENAME.zip.
questions.e: S3 historically partitioned by key prefix, and keys starting with similar characters (sequential, timestamps, same folder prefix) concentrate requests on one partition. Putting a random hex hash at the start of the key, here the folder name, distributes keys across partitions to support thousands of requests per second. Newer S3 scales per prefix automatically, but this was the best practice for this question. (Answer as marked in the Ditectrev repository; not independently verified.)
